findings.title: First-buy dedup and conviction medians live only in process memory — every restart silently shifts the recorded estimand
findings.detail: FirstBuyDedup is a plain in-process set (copy_watcher.py:444-457) instantiated fresh at each boot for the chain path (:551) and separately for RTDS (:803). Nothing rehydrates it from the shadow sink, so after any restart the next repeat BUY by an already-seen (trader, token) pair is recorded with first_buy=true — a false first-buy in the dataset whose stated estimand is 'FIRST BUY per (trader, token)' (:445-447). Likewise TrailingMedians is in-memory (sizing.py:56-79); at boot it is re-seeded from the static copyable_cache (copy_watcher.py:518-526), discarding all live observe() calls since the cache was built, so trailing_median_usd / conviction_r / size_multiplier annotations for the same trader differ before vs after a restart. The contrast is stark: the bidsim registry in the SAME file does rehydrate open state and its dedup (_done) from its sink precisely so 'a restart can never double-register' (copy_watcher.py:1057-1098) — the primary estimand got no such protection. Within mirror_v3, only copy_watcher.py references first_buy (grep verified), so the flag as recorded is the artifact unless an external readout re-derives it.
findings.review_question: Does the downstream readout re-derive first-buy from the full sink (making the recorded flag advisory), or does any analysis consume first_buy as written? Should a rebuild persist dedup/median state (the bidsim rehydrate pattern already exists in-file) or formally declare the flag non-authoritative?
findings.why_it_matters: Under FORWARD DATA ONLY, the shadow log IS the evidence base. If restarts inject false first-buys and shift conviction annotations, the forward dataset's estimand is not stable across the epoch — a rebuild must either persist this state or pin the readout-side re-derivation as canon before any verdict lock consumes it.
findings.verify_note: All cites verified: FirstBuyDedup plain set (copy_watcher.py:444-457), fresh instances at :551 (chain) and :803 (RTDS), no rehydration from the shadow sink anywhere; estimand statement at :445-447. TrailingMedians in-memory (sizing.py:56-79), re-seeded each boot from static cache (copy_watcher.py:518-526) discarding live observe() history. Bidsim contrast confirmed — bidsim_rehydrate seeds _open and _done from its sink, 'a restart can never double-register' (:1057-1098). Grep reproduced: within mirror_v3 only copy_watcher.py references first_buy.

findings.title: Boot cursor starts at head+1 (forward-only): every restart permanently drops the downtime window, and the fail-loud design multiplies restarts
findings.detail: At startup the cursor is set to current head + 1 (copy_watcher.py:552 'forward-only') — fills that landed while the process was down are never fetched, with no backfill path. The architecture then deliberately converts many failure modes into restarts: any watcher exception exits the whole process for systemd restart (run.py:125-130), and the watcher cannot even start unless Database.init() and restore_state() succeed (run.py:45-96) even though the watcher itself does no DB writes (:48-50 docstring). So a DB outage, a restore failure, or any unhandled watcher error each cost a detection gap in the canonical stream. Retry-don't-skip (:586-610) protects windows only while the process lives; MAX_WINDOW_RETRIES=5 then skips a window loudly (:602-607) — also permanent sample loss.
findings.review_question: Should a rebuild persist the block cursor (e.g. to the sink or a state file) and backfill from last-processed block on boot? And should the read-only watcher be decoupled from DB-boot success so a DB incident cannot black out detection? Is the gap size per restart ever measured (restart count x mean downtime)?
findings.why_it_matters: Sample loss is invisible in the dataset itself — the sink just has a gap. If forward measurements (fill-quality distribution, gate rates) are compared across epochs with different restart frequencies, unquantified gaps bias the comparison; a rebuild decision needs to know whether gaps are negligible or structural.
findings.verify_note: cursor = head+1 '# forward-only' at :552, no backfill path exists. run.py:125-130 exits process on watcher-task death; boot requires db.init() success (run.py:46-50, return 3) and restore_state() success (:91-96, return 1) before the watcher starts at :104+. Retry-don't-skip :586-610 with MAX_WINDOW_RETRIES=5 loud skip :602-607 confirmed. One citation ambiguity: the ':48-50 docstring' (no DB writes) reads as run.py:48-50 (which is the DB-init-failed check) but resolves correctly to copy_watcher.py:48-50 ('no DB writes'); run.py:102 comment corroborates.

findings.title: 'shadow_fill' means: full copy size fills at best ask, quoted at an unrecorded moment after variable per-signal RPC work
findings.detail: evaluate_gates returns best_ask as the shadow fill (copy_watcher.py:241-265) — size-blind top-of-book, with the ladder captured but explicitly excluded from verdicts ('gating stays on /price exactly as deployed', :41-46, :488-499). The per-signal pipeline runs sequentially: receipt fetch, block fetch, median update, THEN quote_book (:624-680), each RPC under a 90s timeout (:302,:305-317). detect_ts is stamped at :624 before the receipt fetch, but the ask is quoted at :672 — potentially seconds-to-minutes later in a burst or on a slow RPC — and shadow_record has no quote_ts field (:389-405), so the staleness of the quoted ask relative to detect_ts is unmeasurable from the record. The fill also assumes zero queue/latency between quoting and our hypothetical order landing.
findings.review_question: How large is the detect_ts-to-quote gap in practice (measurable forward by adding a quote_ts field), and does the readout price fills via the VWAP ladder walk as intended or via the top-of-book shadow_fill? Should a rebuild parallelize receipt/block/quote or quote FIRST so the fill quote is as close to detection as the instrument's whole point requires?
findings.why_it_matters: The lane exists to answer exactly one question — does the edge survive real spreads at our latency (:6-13). If the quoted ask is systematically staler than the recorded lag implies, the fill-quality dataset flatters or damns the edge by an unmeasured amount; this goes to the heart of whether the forward evidence is trustworthy.
findings.verify_note: Verified: evaluate_gates returns size-blind best_ask (:241-265, no size param); ladder excluded from verdicts (:41-46, fetch_book fail-soft :488-499); sequential receipt(:628)→block(:645)→medians(:665-668)→quote(:672); RPC_TIMEOUT_S=90 (:302, :305-317); shadow_record has no quote_ts (:389-405). One mechanism nit: detect_ts (now) is stamped per-signal at :624 inside the loop, so burst queueing inflates the RECORDED detect_lag_s rather than the detect_ts→quote gap; the unmeasured gap per signal is bounded by receipt+block RPC (up to ~2×90s) — 'seconds-to-minutes' holds via slow RPC, not via burst queueing.

findings.title: Gate knobs max_chase=2c, max_spread=5c, poll_s=2 have no stated measurement provenance; max_fill=98c is the only knob with one
findings.detail: Defaults: MIRROR3_MAX_CHASE_C=2, MIRROR3_MAX_SPREAD_C=5, MIRROR3_POLL_S=2 (copy_watcher.py:58-62, :337-341, :375-378). Neither the docstring nor the config cites any measurement for 2c chase or 5c spread — contrast max_fill, which carries full provenance (281/3,257 OK first-buys at >=0.999, the 2%-fee zero-upside bound; :243-256). These two unprovenanced knobs directly partition every signal into OK vs PRICE_RAN_AWAY vs SPREAD_TOO_WIDE, i.e. they define which shadow fills exist. Additionally the spread gate silently self-disables when best_bid is None (:261 — a one-sided book passes SPREAD_TOO_WIDE unchecked), and the verdict priority order (NO_BOOK > PRICE_NO_UPSIDE > SPREAD_TOO_WIDE > PRICE_RAN_AWAY, :257-265) shapes gate-attribution statistics without that ordering being a documented choice.
findings.review_question: Were 2c/5c ever swept against the recorded sink (the ladders make this fully re-computable offline for wider values, but NOT for tighter ones — records gated out are still recorded, so a sweep IS possible in both directions on verdict fields)? Should the one-sided-book spread bypass be a distinct verdict so its frequency is visible? Is the verdict priority order the one the readout assumes?
findings.why_it_matters: The OK subset is the numerator of every forward edge claim. If the gate thresholds are arbitrary, the measured 'copyable edge' is conditional on unvalidated knobs; a rebuild should either pre-register a sweep or justify the values from the sink before any live-money gate reads the OK population.
findings.verify_note: Defaults verified at :58-62 (env docs), :337-341 (dataclass), :375-378 (from_env). max_fill provenance verified verbatim (:243-256: 281/3,257 OK first-buys at >=0.999, 2%-fee bound p>=0.9804); no measurement cited anywhere in the file for 2c/5c. Spread gate self-disable on best_bid None confirmed at :261; verdict priority NO_BOOK>PRICE_NO_UPSIDE>SPREAD_TOO_WIDE>PRICE_RAN_AWAY confirmed :257-265 with no documented ordering rationale.

findings.title: Detection rests on a reverse-engineered UNNAMED event on two hardcoded contract addresses — a venue migration re-creates the proven 33h-blind failure class, and a roster-only partial migration would be fully silent
findings.detail: The V1->V2 migration already blinded the watcher once for 33h with zero errors (copy_watcher.py:15-19). Current detection filters FILL_TOPIC_V2 (an unnamed, empirically decoded event, :100-102, :179-186) on exactly two hardcoded addresses (:98-99, :516-517). The blind-RPC canary counts the SAME topic on the SAME addresses (:540-548, :566-583), so: (a) a full venue migration to a V3 contract would trip the canary but with the wrong diagnosis ('Change MIRROR3_RPC_URL', :437-440); (b) a partial migration — roster traders adopting a new contract while legacy flow continues — keeps the canary green while roster detection quietly starves, the exact silent-degrade shape the canary was built to prevent. The was_taker flag also rests on an unvalidated heuristic (topics[3] == emitting exchange, :199-200) whose provenance is not stated, unlike the price layout (validated to 4 decimals, :20-21).
findings.review_question: Should the canary (or a second one) compare roster fill counts against an independent source (data-api or RTDS) so partial migrations and roster-specific blindness are detectable? Is there a watch on Polymarket contract deployments? Was was_taker ever validated, and does anything downstream consume it?
findings.why_it_matters: This is the lane's proven catastrophic failure mode — it has already happened once and cost 33h of the forward epoch. A rebuild must decide whether chain-log decoding of an unnamed event remains the canonical source or whether the RTDS A/B (which is venue-API-level and migration-immune) should be promoted, which is precisely the pending source-swap decision.
findings.verify_note: All cites verified: 33h V1-blind incident (:15-19, 179 missed BUYs), unnamed FILL_TOPIC_V2 (:100-102), decode :179-186, two hardcoded addresses :98-99 used at :516-517, canary queries the SAME topic on the SAME addresses (:540-548, :570), alarm text diagnoses only the RPC (:437-440). Both migration scenarios follow from the code: full migration zeroes canary counts (wrong diagnosis); partial migration keeps legacy V2 flow feeding the canary while roster detection starves. was_taker heuristic at :199-200 has no stated validation, vs price layout validated to 4 decimals (:20-21).

findings.title: Single RPC endpoint is a hard SPOF: no failover, provider-specific quirks baked into the loop, remediation is manual
findings.detail: One rpc_url (copy_watcher.py:334, :55-56 — with a note that publicnode 403s, i.e. alternatives were already found unreliable) serves head fetch, log windows, receipts, and blocks. There is no secondary endpoint or rotation; the canary's remediation is a human changing MIRROR3_RPC_URL and restarting (:437-440), which combined with the forward-only cursor (:552) means every RPC incident costs the full human-response time in dropped samples. Tenderly-specific behavior is load-bearing in the design: the retry-don't-skip logic exists for Tenderly's balancer racing its own head (:586-592), the 33h empty-logs incident was Tenderly (:80-84), and GETLOGS_CHUNK=900 is calibrated to public-RPC caps (:78).
findings.review_question: Should a rebuild support an RPC fallback list with automatic rotation on canary alarm (turning a blindness incident from human-latency loss into seconds), and how much of the loop's retry logic is Tenderly-shaped assumptions that would silently misbehave on a different provider?
findings.why_it_matters: Detection availability is the denominator of the forward dataset. A single third-party gateway, already implicated in two distinct failure modes, controlling 100% of the canonical stream is the largest availability risk in the lane; the rebuild should decide failover vs. RTDS-promotion explicitly.
findings.verify_note: Verified: single rpc_url (:334, env doc :55-56 noting publicnode 403s), no secondary/rotation anywhere in the file, manual remediation in the canary alarm (:437-440), forward-only cursor :552, Tenderly balancer rationale for retry-don't-skip (:586-592), 33h incident was Tenderly (:80-84), GETLOGS_CHUNK=900 public-RPC cap (:78). Minor scope note: 'every RPC incident' is accurate for canary-level blindness/outages; transient errors are absorbed by retry (≤5) without loss.

findings.title: quote_book and fetch_book swallow every exception — a CLOB API outage is recorded as NO_BOOK, indistinguishable from genuinely unquotable markets, with no rate alarm
findings.detail: quote_book catches bare Exception per side and returns None (copy_watcher.py:472-484); evaluate_gates maps a None ask to NO_BOOK (:257-258); fetch_book likewise returns None on any error (:493-499, fail-soft by declared design). There is no counter, streak detector, or alarm on NO_BOOK frequency — unlike the RPC path, which got a canary for exactly this class of silent blindness (:80-91) and the /price semantics path, which got the crossed-book sanity alarm (:408-423). During a CLOB outage every roster signal in the window is permanently recorded as an ungated skip; the dataset cannot later distinguish 'market had no book' from 'our HTTP failed'. Note also the crossed-book guard only catches ask<bid — a semantics change that does not cross (e.g. both sides returning the same side) passes silently (:419).
findings.review_question: Should the record distinguish quote-transport-failure from empty-book (e.g. an error field), and should a NO_BOOK streak have its own canary consistent with the file's stated philosophy that 'an instrument must be able to notice it has gone blind' (:417)? What is the historical NO_BOOK rate and is it stationary?
findings.why_it_matters: NO_BOOK signals are excluded from the fill-quality numerator. If outage-driven NO_BOOKs correlate with volatile periods (when CLOB load spikes), the OK subset is selection-biased toward calm markets — a directional bias in the exact forward measurement the lane exists to make.
findings.verify_note: Verified: bare 'except Exception: px = None' per side in quote_book (:472-484), None ask -> NO_BOOK (:257-258), fetch_book fail-soft (:488-499). Confirmed by full-file read: no counter/streak/alarm exists on NO_BOOK frequency, vs the RPC canary (:80-91) and crossed-book alarm (:408-423). Crossed-book guard fires only on ask<bid (:418-419); the record stores identical null bid/ask for outage vs no-book, so the streams are indeed indistinguishable post hoc.

findings.title: RTDS source-swap rests on unmeasured identity and side-semantics assumptions; a dead RTDS task is never restarted in-process
findings.detail: The chain path derives side from receipt transfer logs relative to the roster trader (copy_watcher.py:210-238, :625-642) and detects the roster as maker OR taker. The RTDS path instead trusts the feed's side field raw (:893-894) and matches roster addresses against proxyWallet (:891); was_taker is declared 'unknowable from this feed' (:772-774), which leaves open whether RTDS emits rows for BOTH legs of a match or only the taker — if only the taker, roster maker-side buys are structurally invisible to RTDS, an estimand gap no tx-level A/B join can reveal (joined rows match; the question is the rows that never appear). proxyWallet == on-chain order-owner (topics[2]) equivalence is assumed, not documented as verified. The two streams also deliberately keep separate dedup and medians (:709-710), so first_buy and conviction annotations are non-identical by construction. Operationally, rtds_watch never raises out (:790-958), so run.py treats .done() as a code bug and only logs it every heartbeat without restarting the task or the process (run.py:112-121, :131-134) — an A/B data gap that persists until the next unrelated full restart.
findings.review_question: Before any source swap: measure (a) the count of chain-detected roster BUYs absent from RTDS (maker-leg coverage), (b) side-label agreement on tx-joined rows, (c) proxyWallet vs order-owner equivalence across the full roster. And should a dead RTDS task self-restart in-process rather than log-and-persist-dead?
findings.why_it_matters: RTDS is the designated successor source (p50 0.82s vs chain 1.30s, and immune to contract migrations). Swapping to it with an unmeasured coverage hole would change the estimand silently — the exact class of error the lane's verdict-lock discipline exists to prevent. The measurements are cheap forward additions to the existing A/B.
findings.verify_note: Headline claims verified: chain path derives side from receipts and catches maker OR taker (:210-238, :625-642, was_taker :199-200); RTDS trusts feed side raw (:893-894) and matches proxyWallet (:891); was_taker 'unknowable from this feed' (:772-774); separate dedup/medians by design (:709-710); rtds_watch never raises out except CancelledError (:790-958); run.py only logs a .done() RTDS task every heartbeat, never restarts it (run.py:112-121, :131-134). One sub-claim overstated: 'no tx-level A/B join can reveal' the maker-leg gap — an anti-join/coverage comparison of the two sinks WOULD surface chain-only rows (chain rows carry was_taker for attribution); only matched-row parity checks are blind to it.

findings.title: No whale-size floor anywhere in the v3 watcher — a $0.01 roster fill is a full signal with quotes, gates, and a conviction multiplier
findings.detail: decode_fill_v2 accepts any fill with tok>0 and usdc>0 (copy_watcher.py:196-197); evaluate_gates takes no size input (:241-244); sizing applies a flat 1-unit base to every approved copy with no minimum (sizing.py:43-53, docstring :6-8). The legacy MB had a $5 whale gate (CLAUDE.md, Key Architecture Facts / MirrorBot traps). Dust fills therefore enter the forward dataset as first-buys on equal footing with conviction bets — they consume the dedup slot for that (trader, token), meaning a $0.05 probe fill permanently marks the pair non-first even if the trader's real position entry lands minutes later in a different tx, and they can dominate OK-population counts.
findings.evidence: C:/lockes-picks/mb-steward/mirror_v3/copy_watcher.py:196-197, :241-244; C:/lockes-picks/mb-steward/mirror_v3/sizing.py:6-8, :43-53; CLAUDE.md section 'Key Architecture Facts' ($5 whale gate)
findings.review_question: Is floorlessness a deliberate pre-registered choice (record everything, filter at readout) or an omission? What fraction of recorded first-buys are sub-$5, and does the first-buy-slot-consumption interaction (dust probe eats the pair's first_buy) bias the estimand? Would a rebuild filter at detection or at readout?
findings.why_it_matters: If dust fills are common among rostered traders (probing is a known whale pattern), the 'first BUY' the dataset grades may systematically be the probe rather than the position — a mismatch with the walk-forward grader's estimand that no forward measurement will self-correct without an explicit check.
findings.verify_note: Code claims fully verified: decode_fill_v2 accepts any tok>0/usdc>0 (:196-197), evaluate_gates has no size input (:241-244), sizing has flat 1-unit base with no minimum (sizing.py docstring :4-8, conviction_multiplier :43-53), and a dust fill does permanently consume the (trader,token) dedup slot (:650-651, :897-898). Citation failure: the '$5 whale gate' is NOT in CLAUDE.md 'Key Architecture Facts' — verified absent from the entire mb-steward CLAUDE.md (case-insensitive grep, section read at :228-238). The legacy fact itself is real but documented in MEMORY.md (Critical Traps, MirrorBot line), so the claim stands with the source corrected.

findings.title: Conviction tiers are declared 'set blind to data' with a pre-registered live-money gate that exists only in prose — the rebuild must preserve both facts
findings.detail: sizing.py's docstring states the tier structure (r>=2 -> 1.25x, r>=4 -> 1.5x, window 50, cold-start lock at 20 obs) was operator-decided blind to data (sizing.py:1-8, constants :34-40), and that the live-money gate — pooled Spearman rho>0, P>=0.95, >=100 resolved fills — is 'pre-registered, not enforced here' (:19-23): in the shadow the multiplier only annotates. Nothing in code enforces the gate; it lives in docs/MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md and this docstring. The annotations feeding that future test are also subject to the restart-drift problem (finding 1) and the chain-vs-RTDS per-row difference (copy_watcher.py:776-778).
findings.review_question: Where is the Option-D gate's canonical pre-registration recorded, and which stream's annotations (chain, with same-tx merge) are the declared test input? Does the rebuild carry the blind-tiers provenance forward verbatim so no one 'tunes' the tiers on the shadow data before the test runs?
findings.why_it_matters: The tiers-set-blind property is what makes the forward conviction test legitimate under FORWARD DATA ONLY — retuning tiers on shadow data before the test would invalidate it. A rebuild that re-derives tier constants from the sink would silently destroy the pre-registration; reviewers need this flagged as preserve-exactly.
findings.verify_note: Verified: 'tiers set blind to data' + docs/MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md decision record (sizing.py:1-8; file exists), constants :34-40, gate 'pre-registered, not enforced here' with Spearman rho>0 / P>=0.95 / >=100 resolved fills, annotate-only (:19-23). Confirmed no enforcement code exists in sizing.py or copy_watcher.py. Annotation sites :665-671 and per-row chain-vs-RTDS divergence note :776-778 verified; restart-drift dependency matches finding 1.

findings.title: Bidsim's fill rule is queue-optimistic by declared design, its band and expiry constants cite a design doc not a measurement, and the trigger-tx exclusion covers only one tx
findings.detail: BIDSIM_LO/HI=0.65/0.85 and BIDSIM_EXPIRE_S=24h (copy_watcher.py:961-970) cite docs/BIDSIM_DESIGN.md; the fill rule fills every open bid at any print <= bid, explicitly bracketing understatement from the other direction (queue-optimistic, :966-967). The 2026-08-21 amendment excludes only the single trigger transaction from filling its own bid (:987-989, :1018-1022) — but a whale sweeping a level across several txs seconds apart would have the SECOND tx 'fill' our shadow bid, when in reality our order would have been behind the same resting queue that tx consumed. The code itself flags 'which side of the tape legitimately fills a resting bid' as an open question, recording print identity so it is 'measurable from forward data rather than assumed' (:1013-1017). Note bidsim is the one component with correct restart persistence (:1057-1098).
findings.review_question: Is the multi-tx-sweep optimism bounded (e.g. by measuring fills whose fill_tx trader equals the trigger trader within N seconds), and what is the pre-registered decision rule that bidsim results feed — maker-vs-taker execution choice for the live copier? Why 0.65-0.85 and 24h — design-doc reasoning or measured?
findings.why_it_matters: If the overhaul considers maker execution (posting at the whale's price instead of crossing), bidsim is the evidence. An optimistic-by-construction fill rate that is not explicitly bracketed against a pessimistic bound can make maker execution look free, steering the rebuild's execution architecture on a one-sided estimate.
findings.verify_note: Two of three clauses verified: queue-optimistic by declared design (:964-967 and BIDSIM_DESIGN.md 'Known biases'), and the exclusion covers only the single trigger transaction (:987-989, on_print :1018-1022; AMENDMENT 1 confirms scope), so the multi-tx sweep critique is sound and the code itself flags the open question (:1013-1017). But the 'not a measurement' clause is contradicted for the band: BIDSIM_DESIGN.md grounds [0.65,0.85) in the measured 2026-08-19 snapshot study (proxy floor 47.6%, break-even ~74%, taker edge +0.0756 vs maker conditional +0.1022, n=131) — measurement provenance exists one hop away, unlike the truly unprovenanced 2c/5c knobs. Only the 24h expiry is confirmed as 'a design choice'.

findings.title: The entire forward dataset is bare append-only JSONL files: no rotation, no fsync, no backup, written with blocking I/O on the event loop
findings.detail: Every record is written by open(path,'a') + write + close inline in the async loops (copy_watcher.py:684-685 chain sink, :940-941 rtds sink, :1114-1116 bidsim sink). There is no explicit flush/fsync policy (interpreter buffering is flushed at close, but OS-level durability on power loss is unguaranteed), no rotation or size management (bidsim_rehydrate re-reads the whole file at every boot, :1061-1078, cost grows unboundedly), no checksums, and — within mirror_v3 — no backup or archival mechanism (grep: only copy_watcher.py references the sink). The files live on a single VPS disk at /opt/pa2-shared/ (:57, :335). A disk-full condition would raise inside the per-signal try-less write on the chain path — which, being outside the per-window except blocks, would kill the watcher task and exit the process (run.py:125-130), turning a full disk into a detection outage.
findings.review_question: Is there any off-VPS backup of the sinks (the epoch's entire evidence, unrecoverable if lost), what is current sink size and growth rate vs disk, and should a rebuild add rotation-with-manifest plus an on-write failure mode that alarms without killing detection?
findings.why_it_matters: The sinks are the irreplaceable output of a months-long $0-risk experiment protected by immutable epochs — a single disk failure erases the evidence the whole overhaul decision depends on. Durability of the dataset deserves the same engineering attention the code gives to detection liveness.
findings.verify_note: Verified: synchronous open/write/close inline in async loops at :684-685 (chain), :940-941 (rtds), :1114-1116 (bidsim); no fsync/rotation/checksum anywhere; bidsim_rehydrate re-reads the whole sink each boot (:1061-1078); paths under /opt/pa2-shared (:57, :335). Grep reproduced: only copy_watcher.py references the sink within mirror_v3 (BIDSIM_DESIGN.md records one manual parked-sample copy, not a mechanism). Disk-full kill path confirmed: the chain-path write has no enclosing try (the per-window excepts end at :598), so an OSError propagates out of watch() and run.py:125-130 exits the process.

findings.title: Two verdict machineries coexist; new single-look tests are still minted on the bar MB_STATE itself diagnosed as structurally underpowered
findings.detail: cohort5_qualification.py grades every trader against EDGE_BAR=0.02 / P_BAR=0.95 / N_BAR=30, single look, immutably locked at first crossing (cohort5_qualification.py:59-62, 145-156). MB_STATE.md documents that this exact bar design is ~8-10% power and 'the full bar (edge>=+0.02 AND P>=0.95) can NEVER pass for a true edge <= ~+0.022' — P>=0.95 at n=30 requires edge >= +0.127 (MB_STATE.md:419-422, 511-516). The band test was redesigned to an anytime-valid e-process for precisely this reason (band_tracker.py:38-47, BAND_PREREGISTRATION.md 'Test'), yet on 2026-08-24 a NEW registration (C1_UNTESTED, 9 traders, epoch 2026-08-24T17:00Z) was created on the OLD single-look design (cohort5_qualification.py:39-57, 158-163). Locks are immutable, so a trader who fails a structurally unclearable test is permanently locked DOES-NOT-QUALIFY.
findings.review_question: Should the overhaul retire the fixed-n single-look design entirely and migrate all future qualification tests (including C1_UNTESTED, whose window opens today) to the e-process design, before any of the new locks are consumed? What is the policy for locks already consumed under the ~8-10%-power design — do they carry any decision weight in the rebuild?
findings.why_it_matters: A rebuild that inherits the qualification pipeline inherits a test that mathematically cannot pass at economically realistic edges, silently rejecting every borderline-good trader forever (locks are immutable). The system's own docs prove the defect; only one of the two verdict paths was fixed.
findings.verify_note: All citations verify: bars at cohort5_qualification.py:59-62, first-crossing immutable locks at :146-156 (write_lock refuses re-lock, shadow_readout.py:427-439; locked traders skipped as 'single look consumed'); MB_STATE.md:419-426 ('P>=0.95 at n=30 requires edge >= +0.127', 7-8%/8-10% power) and :513-516 (full bar 'can NEVER pass for a true edge <= ~+0.022') quoted accurately; C1_UNTESTED (9 traders, epoch 2026-08-24T17:00Z) at :39-57 graded via the same single-look grade() at :158-163. Two omitted contexts: (1) the extension was an explicit operator directive quoted in the code ('do it if they pass the test', operator go 2026-08-24); (2) 'structurally unclearable' is exact only for true edge <= ~+0.022 — a very large true edge can pass; MB_STATE frames it as ~8-10% power at realistic edges and says the bar 'needs an operator redesign decision'. Core claim stands.

findings.title: Three scripts compute three different 'edge' estimands under the same name
findings.detail: analyze_shadow.analyze pools edges PER-FILL: vals flattens all fills across tokens, so the point estimate is fill-weighted and a token with many roster fills dominates; the bootstrap resamples tokens but each sampled token still contributes all its fills (analyze_shadow.py:214-239, 148-160). band_tracker computes PER-MARKET MEAN edges and weighs each market equally in both the e-process and the pooled economic-gate number (band_tracker.py:75-78, 108-110), matching BAND_PREREGISTRATION's frozen 'per-market mean edge'. cohort5 reuses the per-fill analyze() path per trader (cohort5_qualification.py:137). The same shadow log therefore yields different 'edge' numbers depending on which script reports, and cross-script comparisons (e.g. cohort edge vs band edge) are apples-to-oranges.
findings.review_question: Which weighting (per-fill or per-market) is the estimand the rebuilt bot will actually realize P&L against, and should the overhaul standardize one edge definition across all readouts with the other explicitly renamed (e.g. 'fill-weighted edge')?
findings.why_it_matters: A go/no-go built on numbers that quietly measure different quantities can approve a strategy on one estimand and size it on another. Fill-weighting also lets a single heavily-copied market dominate the cohort verdict — the concentration disclosure covers traders, not markets.
findings.verify_note: Verified: analyze_shadow.py:236-239 flattens all fills (fill-weighted point estimate) and cluster_bootstrap_p (:148-160) resamples tokens but keeps each token's full fill list; band_tracker.py:75-78 takes per-market means and :107-108 weighs markets equally in e-process and pooled gate, matching BAND_PREREGISTRATION's frozen 'per-market mean edge'; cohort5_qualification.py:137 routes through cohort_readout -> analyze (per-fill). Nuance the title overstates slightly: cohort5's FORMULA is the same per-fill one as analyze_shadow — it differs by population (per-trader forward window) and fee model, so it is two weighting schemes across three scripts, though the three do yield mutually incomparable numbers as claimed.

findings.title: Fee-model divergence: a post-2026-08-19 registration (C1_UNTESTED) is graded under the deprecated flat-fee model
findings.detail: analyze_shadow's docstring rules that the venue formula rate*p*(1-p) 'governs diagnostics and post-2026-08-19 registrations' (analyze_shadow.py:176-187). shadow_readout and band_tracker pass fee_rate_map; cohort5_qualification builds its cfg with fee_map_data only and NEVER sets fee_rate_map_data (cohort5_qualification.py:129-130), so all its grading — including the C1_UNTESTED group registered 2026-08-24 — uses the flat 2% model the code itself documents as OVERCHARGING high-priced fills (at p=0.9: 0.018 flat vs 0.0063 true). Since qualification verdicts lock immutably, a trader whose true venue-fee edge clears +0.02 can be permanently DQ'd by the fee-model choice. band_tracker additionally hardcodes the 0.02 flat fallback inline (band_tracker.py:74) instead of taking it from config.
findings.review_question: Should cohort5_qualification adopt fee_rate_map before the C1_UNTESTED window accrues its first 30 resolved markets, and does the overhaul define ONE canonical fee function that every verdict script imports rather than three re-implementations of the precedence chain?
findings.why_it_matters: Fees are the difference between +0.02 passing and failing at mid-high fill prices (flat charges 0.015/share at p=0.75 vs venue 0.0094); immutable locks convert a fee-model inconsistency into a permanent roster decision.
findings.verify_note: Verified: analyze_shadow.py:186-187 says the venue formula 'governs diagnostics and post-2026-08-19 registrations only'; cohort5_qualification.py:129-130 builds cfg with fee_map_data only, never fee_rate_map_data, so cohort_readout's getattr (shadow_readout.py:268) passes None and all cohort5/C1 grading falls back to flat 2% (measured-zero tokens exempt); the p=0.9 overcharge numbers are quoted verbatim from :185-187; band_tracker.py:74 hardcodes 0.02 inline. Context: COHORT5_PREREGISTRATION.md deliberately FROZE the flat-fee equation for cohort5 ('registered HERE... a calibrated RATE... would apply only to cohorts registered after it') — so flat fee is by design for the original 2026-07-30 arms; the tension is real specifically for C1_UNTESTED (registered 2026-08-24, after the rate map existed), which is exactly what the finding targets.

findings.title: Guard asymmetry: band_tracker and cohort5 bypass the zero-row-supplement refusal and the fee-map validation/disclosure that shadow_readout treats as FATAL
findings.detail: shadow_readout refuses to read out when the supplement labels 0 shadow tokens (the 'flattered DB-only' failure mode, 2026-07-22) and FATALs on empty/corrupt fee maps, printing a fee_note either way (shadow_readout.py:486-504, 511-537). supplement_outcomes itself returns {} when the cache has entries but none touch the token set — the zero-row guard lives in the CALLER. band_tracker.py:87 and cohort5_qualification.py:124 call supplement_outcomes with no zero-row check, so both can silently degrade to DB-only labels — the exact mechanism measured to flatter cohort edges by +0.03 (shadow_readout.py:15-26). band_tracker also loads both fee maps with a bare os.path.exists fallback to {} and prints NO fee-model disclosure at all (band_tracker.py:89-92): a deleted/renamed fee_rate_map.json silently flips the band test to the flat model mid-experiment.
findings.review_question: Should the overhaul centralize label-loading and fee-loading (with the refusal + disclosure semantics) into one shared function all three verdict scripts must go through, instead of each new script re-deciding which guards to copy?
findings.why_it_matters: The 07-22 landmine proved a silent label shortfall produces a confident, flattered edge. The guard was built, but only in one of three verdict scripts — the two NEWEST tests (band, cohort5) can reproduce the exact failure the guard exists to prevent, and their outputs feed lock files.
findings.verify_note: Verified: shadow_readout.py:486-504 refuses on a supplement that labels 0 tokens and :511-537 FATALs on empty/corrupt fee maps with a fee_note always printed; supplement_outcomes (:215-227) raises only on missing/unreadable/empty file and returns {} when no entries touch the token set — the zero-row guard is caller-side; band_tracker.py:87 and cohort5_qualification.py:124 call it with no zero-row check; band_tracker.py:89-92 loads both fee maps with bare os.path.exists->{} fallback and prints no fee-model disclosure anywhere. The +0.03 flattering figure matches cohort1 +0.0604->+0.0315 in shadow_readout.py:15-26. Fair note the finding already implies: a MISSING supplement file still fails loud in both scripts (uncaught SupplementError); the silent-degrade path is specifically the zero-matching-rows case.

findings.title: First-crossing locks and anytime e-process looks are taken on a resolution-timing-selected subset; the proven precedent is that the missing slice is systematically negative
findings.detail: Cohort verdicts lock at the FIRST run where resolved_mkts >= 30 (shadow_readout.py:604-614); the band verdict locks at the first run with e >= 20 (band_tracker.py:113-125). Both interim snapshots include only markets that have RESOLVED AND been LABELLED by then. The 2026-07-22 finding (shadow_readout.py:15-26) established that the unlabelled slice was 'systematically NEGATIVE' and flattered every reported edge. Label lag is partially mitigated by shadow_label_supplement, but that job is dry-run by default and requires --write (shadow_label_supplement.py:221-234) — its cron cadence determines how stale labels are at lock time. Resolution-TIMING selection (fast-resolving sports vs long-dated markets) is not mitigated at all: a verdict can lock on the early-resolving subset and is then immutable when slower markets land.
findings.review_question: Is the supplement job actually cron-scheduled with --write ahead of every readout/band run (measure the gap), and should lock entries record label-completeness at lock time (unlabelled-token count) so a lock consumed on a label-lagged snapshot is auditable — or should locking require unlabelled-fraction below a threshold?
findings.why_it_matters: The stopping rule was built to prevent optional stopping by the ANALYST, but the DATA can still stop optionally: if negatives resolve or label late, 'first crossing' is systematically the most flattering moment, and the immutable lock then freezes that bias into the roster/scale decision.
findings.verify_note: Verified: cohort lock at first resolved_mkts >= min_markets (default 30, shadow_readout.py:604-614, :1108); band lock at first e>=20 or futility 600 (band_tracker.py:112-125); outcomes maps contain only resolved+labelled markets by construction; the 2026-07-22 'systematically NEGATIVE' unlabelled-slice finding is at shadow_readout.py:15-26; shadow_label_supplement.py:221-223 is dry-run unless --write. One softening point: the band e-process's type-I error remains valid under resolution-order arrival (anytime-validity covers the stopping rule under H0); the unmitigated exposure is estimand/generalization and the economic gate computed on the early-resolving subset — plus the fixed-n cohort look, where the concern applies fully. MB_STATE's own caveats acknowledge chronology imperfection. Claim is fair as stated.

findings.title: DB-wins label merge has no conflict detection — a wrong DB resolution silently overrides the CLOB-verified supplement
findings.detail: merge_outcomes applies dict.update: DB always wins, and no disagreement between DB and supplement is counted or printed (shadow_readout.py:230-236). label_provenance discloses DB/supp/unlabelled counts but not conflicts (shadow_readout.py:239-247). By contrast, the cache-build side treats a disagreement as a loud CONFLICT left for a human (shadow_label_supplement.py:86-98). The precedence rationale ('DB is the system's own settled record') assumed DB labels are incomplete but never wrong; a bad markets.resolution row would flip both legs of a market's outcome with zero trace, directly moving edge and possibly a locked verdict.
findings.review_question: Should merge_outcomes count and print DB-vs-supplement disagreements (and refuse or flag when nonzero), matching the CONFLICT semantics the supplement writer already has?
findings.why_it_matters: Label integrity is this pipeline's proven weak point (two prior landmines). The one merge point where the two independent sources meet is exactly where a corruption check is cheapest, and it currently reports nothing.
findings.verify_note: Verified exactly: merge_outcomes (shadow_readout.py:230-236) is dict(supp); merged.update(db) with no disagreement count; label_provenance (:239-247) prints DB/supp/unlabelled only; the docstring rationale 'The DB is the system's own settled record; the supplement exists solely because the backfill structurally cannot see shadow markets' assumes incompleteness, not wrongness; shadow_label_supplement.merge_entry (:86-98) returns 'CONFLICT' and the run loop prints each conflicted cid without overwriting — the loud-conflict behavior exists only on the cache-build side.

findings.title: Shadow fill is top-of-book ask with depth ignored; the +0.02 economic floor is per-share with no size/capacity model
findings.detail: repair_record derives shadow_fill as the single lowest ask price; ladder SIZE fields are present in the records but never read (analyze_shadow.py:88-105 — min over price only). Every downstream number — copy tax (analyze_shadow.py:194-195), edge (:235), the band e-process (band_tracker.py:61-75) — assumes the full copy executes at best ask. The econ floor +0.02 (analyze_shadow.py:352) is a per-share quantity; nothing in the pipeline estimates fillable size at that price, so a 'SURVIVES' verdict certifies an edge that may only exist for the first few dollars of depth.
findings.review_question: Before a live-capital decision, should the pipeline compute a depth-weighted fill (walk the recorded ladder for the intended order size) and report edge-at-size alongside edge-at-touch — and what order size does the rebuild intend, so the estimand can match it?
findings.why_it_matters: This is the gap between a measurement verdict and a money verdict: the ladders needed to compute edge-at-size are already being recorded, but the verdict pipeline discards them, so a pass could evaporate at the first realistically-sized order. (docs/BIDSIM_DESIGN.md exists and may cover this — the review should reconcile.)
findings.verify_note: Verified: repair_record takes min over ladder prices only (analyze_shadow.py:88-89); grep confirms 'size' appears in analyze_shadow.py only inside self-test fixture data, never read in the pipeline; copy tax (:194-195), edge (:235), band e-process inputs (band_tracker.py:61-78) all assume full execution at best ask; econ floor default 0.02 at :352 is per-share. No size/depth model exists in any of the three verdict scripts. Claim accurate and not exaggerated.

findings.title: Band test population is not roster-gated in code, though the frozen estimand says 'ALL clean-roster traders'
findings.detail: BAND_PREREGISTRATION.md's frozen estimand pools 'across ALL clean-roster traders'. band_tracker never loads the roster: band_market_edges filters only on forward window, first_buy, OK verdict, and band membership (band_tracker.py:55-78); run() applies no trader filter (:81-100). Any record in mirror3_shadow.jsonl counts — including fills from traders benched or removed from 'clean' mid-window, and any probe/scout stream the watcher writes to the same file. Roster changes therefore silently change the population of a locked, running pre-registered test.
findings.review_question: Does the shadow JSONL ever contain non-clean-roster records in the forward window (measureable now), and should band_tracker filter to the roster's clean set — or is 'whatever the watcher logged' the intended population, in which case the pre-registration wording should be corrected before the verdict locks?
findings.why_it_matters: A code-vs-registration estimand mismatch on a live immutable-lock test is exactly the class of dispute a verdict lock cannot survive; resolving it after e crosses 20 would look like moving the goalposts no matter which way it is resolved.
findings.verify_note: Verified: BAND_PREREGISTRATION.md freezes 'pooled across ALL clean-roster traders'; band_tracker never loads chain_audit.json or any roster — band_market_edges (:55-78) filters only on forward window/first_buy/OK/band, and run() (:81-100) applies no trader filter, so every record in the JSONL counts. Minor nuance: 'benched' addresses are part of the roster's clean union per shadow_readout's ledger check, so whether pooling them violates the frozen wording is arguable; but a trader removed from clean mid-window, or any other stream written to the same file, would silently count — the code-level fact is confirmed.

findings.title: C1_UNTESTED membership is hardcoded in the script, violating the pipeline's own 'membership from the roster file, NEVER hardcoded' rule
findings.detail: cohort5_qualification.py:47-57 embeds 9 addresses as a module constant with their own epoch. shadow_readout.load_cohorts exists precisely because hardcoded/implicit membership caused the 2026-07-15 silent-pooling defect ('Membership comes from the file, NEVER hardcoded', shadow_readout.py:74-93), and it enforces overlap/duplicate/clean-union guards. The hardcoded group bypasses all of those: if one of the 9 is benched or admitted to a cohort in chain_audit.json, this tracker keeps grading them with no cross-check, and its locks file shares a namespace with chain-ADMIT locks keyed only by address (grade(), :134-156).
findings.review_question: Should C1_UNTESTED move into chain_audit.json (or its own ledger key) so the roster consistency guards cover it, and should the shared cohort5_qual_locks.json record which test (cohort5 vs cohort1-untested) consumed each address's single look?
findings.why_it_matters: The roster ledger is the single source of truth the whole guard architecture hangs on; a second, code-resident membership list reintroduces the drift class those guards were built to kill, in the script that mints permanent qualification verdicts.
findings.verify_note: Verified: 9 addresses as a module constant with own epoch (cohort5_qualification.py:47-57); shadow_readout.load_cohorts docstring (:74-93) states 'Membership comes from the file, NEVER hardcoded' citing the 2026-07-15 silent-pooling defect, and enforces duplicate/overlap/clean-union guards (:138-159) that the hardcoded group bypasses; both grade() calls share one locks file keyed only by address (:131-163). No cross-check against chain_audit.json exists. Context: the 9 are documented in-code as never chain-ADMITted (so overlap is unexpected at registration) and the group has its own self-test (:202-205) — but the finding's benched/later-admitted drift scenario is unguarded, as claimed.

findings.title: Cohort5 grades ~29 per-trader arms at raw P>=0.95 with no multiplicity control — the correction shadow_readout itself documents as necessary
findings.detail: eligible_admits yields ~20 chain-ADMITs plus the 9 hardcoded C1_UNTESTED, each graded single-look at P_BAR=0.95 (cohort5_qualification.py:59-62, 134-163). Under a null of zero edge for all arms, expected false qualifiers ≈ 29 × 0.05 ≈ 1.45. shadow_readout's per-trader diagnostic explicitly applies a Bonferroni-adjusted bar for exactly this reason ('among N arms it is unremarkable', shadow_readout.py:290-299) — but that reasoning was applied only to the DIAGNOSTIC display, not to the qualification test where arms produce real roster proposals. The pre-registration (COHORT5_PREREGISTRATION.md) presumably ratified per-trader bars, so this may be a deliberate, operator-accepted tradeoff — but the tension between the two scripts is in the code.
findings.review_question: Was per-arm alpha (no family-wise control) an explicit choice in COHORT5_PREREGISTRATION.md, and if so does the overhaul want a portfolio-level guard instead (e.g. cap on simultaneous qualifiers, or a cohort-level confirmation test post-composition) rather than tightening per-arm P?
findings.why_it_matters: Roster composition is the bot's actual alpha source; with ~29 arms and immutable QUALIFIES locks, the pipeline will statistically manufacture one or two false-positive traders even if nobody has edge, and composition inherits them.
findings.verify_note: Verified: P_BAR=0.95 applied raw per trader with no Bonferroni anywhere in cohort5_qualification.py; eligible ADMITs = 20 per the code docstring and COHORT5_PREREGISTRATION.md ('the 20 current ADMITs qualify') + 9 hardcoded = 29 arms; shadow_readout.py:289-299 applies a Bonferroni-adjusted bar to the per-trader DIAGNOSTIC display for exactly this reason ('among N arms it is unremarkable'). The finding's hedge is confirmed correct: COHORT5_PREREGISTRATION.md criterion 3 operator-ratified the per-trader raw P>=0.95 single look with no multiplicity control mentioned, so this is a pre-registered design choice — and the ~1.45 expected null false-qualifiers arithmetic is consistent with MB_STATE's measured 5.40% one-shot FPR.

findings.title: A second shadow stream (mirror3_shadow_rtds.jsonl) feeds the fee map but not the verdict pipeline
findings.detail: build_fee_map reads both mirror3_shadow.jsonl and mirror3_shadow_rtds.jsonl (build_fee_map.py:143, 274-275), implying an RTDS-sourced record stream exists. shadow_readout (:1070), band_tracker (:166), and cohort5_qualification (:223) default only to mirror3_shadow.jsonl. MB_STATE references 'post (chain AND rtds)' sinks and RTDS fixes raising flow for the band test (BAND_PREREGISTRATION.md 'Expected timeline'). Whether RTDS-detected fills are folded into the main JSONL by the watcher, or live only in the _rtds file and are thus invisible to every verdict, cannot be determined from these scripts alone.
findings.review_question: Measure: does mirror3_shadow_rtds.jsonl contain first-buy records absent from mirror3_shadow.jsonl in the forward windows? If yes, which stream is the pre-registered tests' record source of truth, and do RTDS records carry the fields (book ladders, detect_ts, first_buy) the repair/verdict path requires?
findings.why_it_matters: If the faster detection path's records bypass the verdict pipeline, the measured copy tax and OK-rate describe the SLOWER path the rebuild intends to replace — the readout would be systematically pessimistic (or the population incomplete) for exactly the architecture being decided on.
findings.verify_note: Verified: build_fee_map.py:143 reads both files and :274-275 defaults --shadow-rtds to mirror3_shadow_rtds.jsonl; shadow_readout.py:1070, band_tracker.py:166, and cohort5_qualification.py:223 all default --log to mirror3_shadow.jsonl only; MB_STATE.md:197 contains the quoted 'post (chain AND rtds)' phrase and BAND_PREREGISTRATION's timeline cites RTDS fixes raising flow. Additional context that partly resolves the finding's open question: MB_STATE.md:252-257 documents the _rtds file as a deliberate A/B sink with the 'chain stream canonical + untouched' — so the exclusion appears intentional (A/B, not lost data), though the finding's hedge ('cannot be determined from these scripts alone') already covers this honestly.

findings.title: Gate/repair logic and constants are duplicated across scripts rather than imported from the watcher
findings.detail: repair_record claims 'the gate logic mirrors copy_watcher.evaluate_gates exactly' (analyze_shadow.py:83-85) — a by-hand duplication, so any watcher gate change (constants or a new gate) silently diverges the re-derived verdicts from the live ones. band_tracker hardcodes the repair constants positionally (0.02, 0.05 at band_tracker.py:84) instead of plumbing them; analyze_shadow exposes them as CLI args (:355-356). Similarly, CATEGORY_RATES is a hardcoded schedule snapshot ('fetched 2026-08-19', including geopolitics: 0.0 — an entire category at zero haircut) applied retroactively to all fills via fetch-time (not fill-time) fee reads, and the fee-map merge keeps old per-token entries forever (build_fee_map.py:47-54, 104-112, 211-218) — a venue fee change would be half-applied with no staleness marker in the artifact.
findings.review_question: Should the overhaul make copy_watcher's gate function and one fee module the single imported implementation for both live gating and retrospective repair (as shadow_label_supplement already does for resolution derivation via the production backfill helpers), and should fee artifacts carry a fetched-at stamp with a staleness check at read time?
findings.why_it_matters: The pipeline's credibility rests on the analysis reproducing the live gates exactly; duplicated logic guarantees eventual drift, and a stale zero-rate category (geopolitics 0.0) is a silent edge-flattering channel with no alarm.
findings.verify_note: Verified: 'the gate logic mirrors copy_watcher.evaluate_gates exactly' at analyze_shadow.py:83-85 is by-hand duplication; band_tracker.py:84 hardcodes 0.02/0.05 positionally while analyze_shadow exposes them as CLI args (:355-356); CATEGORY_RATES is a hardcoded 2026-08-19 snapshot incl. geopolitics 0.0 (build_fee_map.py:47-54), fetch_fee reads current (fetch-time) taker_base_fee (:104-112), and the merge keeps old entries for out-of-window tokens with no timestamps in the flat artifact (:211-218, :224-235). The divergence risk is already REALIZED, strengthening the claim: the watcher's 2026-08-19 PRICE_NO_UPSIDE/max_fill gate (MB_STATE.md:486-489) is absent from repair_record, so re-derived verdicts already diverge from live gates.

findings.title: ADMIT grades the TRADER's edge at the trader's own fill prices — no term anywhere in the verdict measures OUR attainable copy price
findings.detail: Tier 3 edge is computed as outcome minus the trader's chain fill price (chain_deep_dive.py:459-460 'edge': o - f['price']). The verdict metrics dict (chain_deep_dive.py:1138-1182) contains no maker/taker, latency, spread, or slippage input; maker_taker_profile is computed (:1007) and reported in tier4_forensics (:1207) but never gated. The lane has already hit this exact gap twice: 0xfbfd14dd was ADMITted with maker_frac=0.886 — edge earned at MAKER prices while MB copies as a TAKER crossing the spread (docs/MB_STATE.md:370-376) — and the 08-19 shadow-fill audit found 8.6% of OK first-buys filled at >=0.999 (281/3,257), i.e. the copy fill can be up to $1.00 regardless of the admitted edge (docs/MB_STATE.md:402-417). The decision/flow/rate gates test mechanical absorbability, not price attainability.
findings.review_question: Should the overhaul add a copy-price-attainability pillar to admission (maker_frac gate, taker-side replay of the trader's entries, max-fill-price bound), or explicitly re-scope ADMIT as integrity-only and leave attainability entirely to the forward shadow?
findings.why_it_matters: This is the core trader-quality-vs-copyability confusion: a trader can be genuinely skilled and still un-copyable at our lag and side of the book. Cohort-3's negative live edge and the $1.00-fill defect are both downstream of admitting on the trader's price, so a rebuild that keeps this verdict shape will keep producing admitted-but-unprofitable cohorts.
findings.verify_note: All citations exact: edge = o - f['price'] at :459-460; metrics dict :1138-1182 has no maker/taker/spread/slippage key (grep confirms mt is used only at :1007/:1049/:1207, never in metrics or deep_dive_verdict); MB_STATE :370-376 (maker_frac=0.886 ADMIT) and :402-417 (281/3,257 = 8.6% OK first-buys shadow-filled >= 0.999, 'no maximum-fill-price gate') say exactly what is claimed. The decision/flow/rate gates indeed test absorbability, not price attainability.

findings.title: The decisive ADMIT pillar (skill_clears) is an in-sample bootstrap grade — zero decision weight under FORWARD DATA ONLY, with no multiplicity control across screened candidates
findings.detail: ADMIT requires the chain-graded record to clear wf.hire_ok — >=25 markets, >=60-day span, bootstrap P(edge>0)>=0.90 on historical per-market edges (chain_deep_dive.py:1631-1634 defaults; walkforward_copy_traders.py:108-118). A non-clearing record routes to INSUFFICIENT (chain_deep_dive.py:563-566), so skill is the main discriminator between ADMIT and INSUFFICIENT. P>=0.90 applied one-trader-at-a-time across multi-dozen rosters (runs 1-4 screened 27-47 candidates, docs/MB_STATE.md:815, :1148) has no family-wise correction; the screen will admit some zero-edge traders by chance. The lane's own downstream structure concedes the point: cohort5_qualification.py:5-8 uses chain-ADMIT only as ELIGIBILITY and qualifies on the FORWARD record — yet historically ADMITs went straight to the live shadow roster (docs/MB_STATE.md:1166-1168).
findings.review_question: Under FORWARD DATA ONLY, should the rebuilt screen drop skill as an admission pillar entirely (keep integrity + mechanical copyability as gates, treat every integrity-clean trader as forward-measurable), and if skill screening is kept for triage, what selection-adjusted bar replaces the raw per-trader P>=0.90?
findings.why_it_matters: The screen's most expensive computation (labels, bootstrap, span) produces exactly the kind of in-sample number the operator has ruled carries zero decision weight. Clarifying what ADMIT is FOR (fraud screen vs quality screen vs eligibility ticket) is the single biggest architectural question for the overhaul.
findings.verify_note: Verified: hire-bar defaults 25/60d/P>=0.90 at :1631-1634; hire_ok bootstrap on historical per-market edges at walkforward :108-118; non-clearing routes to INSUFFICIENT at :563-566; no family-wise correction anywhere in the code; cohort5_qualification :4-8/:65-82 uses chain-ADMIT as eligibility only; MB_STATE :1165-1168 confirms the first 8 ADMITs went straight to the live shadow roster (with an operator go). Two minor caveats: 'zero decision weight under FORWARD DATA ONLY' is the reviewer's application of a lane rule from memory, not text in the cited files; and MB_STATE:815 shows run-4 at 28 traders (run-3 was 27 per :905), so '27-47' is a hair loose but the range claim is supported.

findings.title: The 'chain-truth' verdict conditions on API/DB caches at three load-bearing joints: token->market mapping, resolution labels, and the sweep's low bound
findings.detail: Despite the module framing ('re-graded on CHAIN data — the one source that cannot be faked', chain_deep_dive.py:5-8), only prices/sizes/blocks are chain-sourced. (1) tok2cond is built exclusively from cached API rows (:1071-1072), so any chain first-buy on a token the API record omits gets a synthetic 'tok:' key (:229), cannot be labeled (:452-456), and silently drops out of the skill grade — a trader who hides markets from the API also hides them from the re-grade. (2) Labels come from the DB plus the gamma_resolutions.json cache via markets_loader (:1269-1274, find_copyable_traders.py:169-179). (3) For a complete cache the sweep low bound is first-API-claim minus 14 days (:954-956), with pre-first-claim hidden activity a documented scope limit (:944-945).
findings.review_question: Should the rebuild derive token->condition mapping from chain/CTF data (or gamma by token id) instead of the trader's own API record, so that hidden-market activity can actually lower the grade rather than vanish from it?
findings.why_it_matters: The screen's anti-fraud premise is that the chain record overrides the trader's self-report — but the market universe over which skill is judged is still defined by the self-report. A rebuild decision about what the screen proves needs this dependency map stated honestly.
findings.verify_note: All three joints confirmed: tok2cond built solely from cached API rows (:1071-1072); unmapped tokens get 'tok:' keys (:229) and are unlabelable/dropped from the grade (:451-456); labels from DB + preloaded gamma cache via markets_loader (:1269-1274) using fc.label_outcome (:169-179); complete-cache low bound = first API claim minus pad_days (default 14, :1623) at :954-956 with the pre-first-claim scope limit at :943-945. Minor: 'silently drops out' is slightly strong — n_unlabelable IS reported in tier3_skill output — but the verdict never gates on the unlabelable fraction, so the substantive point holds. Also sides/counterparties are chain-sourced too, not only prices/sizes/blocks; immaterial to the claim.

findings.title: incomplete_cache_sweep is recorded in output but never consulted by the verdict — ADMIT is reachable on a truncated/stale API cache
findings.detail: The incomplete_cache flag (cache_status in hft/truncated/partial/missing, chain_deep_dive.py:949) only changes the sweep low bound (:952-953) and is written to results (:1040, :1186); grep confirms deep_dive_verdict never reads it. The cache-hit path silently reuses any existing <addr>.json without a staleness check unless --refresh is passed (:1285-1290). Consequences already observed: 0xfbfd14dd ADMITted with incomplete_cache_sweep=TRUE (docs/MB_STATE.md:372), and 9 scout candidates had caches stale since 2026-07-10 / truncated to 500 rows that a dive would silently reuse (docs/MB_STATE.md:383-388). On such a cache, Tier-2 backing is computed over only the partial claimed record (min_api_check is just 10 BUYs, :1641-1642) and Direction-B hidden-activity is disabled outright (hidden=null, :1108-1112).
findings.review_question: Should cache completeness/freshness become a hard precondition for ADMIT (e.g. ADMIT only on cache_status=ok fetched within N days), rather than a recorded-but-ignored weakness flag the operator must remember to check?
findings.why_it_matters: An admission gate whose evidentiary base can silently be a 500-row, weeks-old snapshot does not prove what its ADMIT string claims. This is a cheap, high-leverage fix candidate for the rebuild and directly affects whether past ADMITs are comparable to future ones.
findings.verify_note: Grep confirms incomplete_cache appears only at :949/:952/:1040/:1186 — it changes the sweep low bound and is written to results; the metrics dict passed to deep_dive_verdict carries no such key. Cache-hit path (:1285-1290) reuses any existing <addr>.json with no staleness check unless --refresh. MB_STATE :372 (0xfbfd14dd ADMIT with incomplete_cache_sweep=TRUE, both runs) and :382-388 (9 scout caches stale 2026-07-10 / 500-row hft, silent reuse) confirmed. min_api_check=10 (:1641-1642) and hidden=null on incomplete caches (:1099-1112) confirmed.

findings.title: Stale/truncated caches also produce FALSE REJECTs: unmapped tokens inflate decisions/day through the hard decision gate
findings.detail: reconstruct_first_buys keys unmapped tokens as their own 'market' (chain_deep_dive.py:229), and decisions_per_day = len(chain_first_buys)/span (:1117) feeds a HARD REJECT (:543-546). With an hft-truncated cache, tok2cond covers only ~500 recent rows, so lifetime chain tokens each count as a new market — the lane documented this exact FALSE-REJECT mechanism plus the mirror effect (skill deterministically ungradeable, span<60d) for all 34 HFT-borderline candidates (docs/MB_STATE.md:909-915). The applied fix was operational (rename 27 caches to .hft-bak and re-fetch), not a code guard — the mechanism is still live for any future stale cache.
findings.review_question: Should the decision-rate gate refuse to fire (route to INSUFFICIENT) when the unmapped-token fraction among first-buys exceeds a threshold, so a cache artifact can never convert into a hard REJECT?
findings.why_it_matters: REJECT is supposed to be reserved for affirmative chain facts, but this path lets a cache gap masquerade as a measured infeasibility — the exact failure mode the operator's not_found-is-a-gap rule bans. A rebuild keeping these gates needs the guard structural, not procedural.
findings.verify_note: Mechanism verified in code: :229 keys unmapped tokens as their own market, :1117 decisions_per_day over all chain_first_buys, :543-546 hard REJECT. MB_STATE :908-915 documents exactly this ('unmapped tokens inflate decisions/day (each token = a "market") → FALSE-REJECT through the hard decision gate') plus the ADMIT-unreachable mirror effect, and the fix as renaming 27 caches to .hft-bak. Confirmed no code guard was added: post_direction_flags has no cache-status input, and only a MISSING cache triggers a full re-fetch (:1296-1299) — a present-but-stale hft cache is still silently reused.

Reproducibility of locked verdicts is foundational for the pre-registered-epoch discipline the lane runs on.

findings.title: The three UNCOPYABLE thresholds (1000 fills/day, 25 decisions/day, 0.60 flat-share) are calibrated on a single anecdote with no engine-capacity measurement
findings.detail: The 2026-07-16 rework comments justify the parameter SET by one wallet, 0xf705fa (461 fills/day, 7.6 decisions/day, 16% net-flat — chain_deep_dive.py:1650-1653, :495-501); each threshold sits above that wallet with unexplained headroom. receipt-free-rate=1000 (:1654-1657) has no stated derivation. max-decisions-per-day=25 claims 'more decisions than the one-bet-per-market engine absorbs' (:1658-1661) but no measured engine absorption capacity is cited anywhere in the file. max-flat-share=0.60 (:1662-1666) contradicts the module's own rationale that 'a true flow trader is ~90%+ flat' (:332-335) — nothing explains the 0.60-vs-0.90 gap. Secondary unexplained constants: 100-fill sample floor (:399-404), 20-position floor (:414-417 with a documented no-ts_ok asymmetry, test_chain_deep_dive.py:434-440), fabrication_frac=0.50 (:1644-1646), min_api_check=10 / min_api_backing=0.80 (:1641-1643), wash_share=0.50 (:1648), tol_price=0.02 / tol_size=0.05 (:1636-1637).
findings.review_question: For each hard-REJECT threshold, what is the derivation the rebuild should demand — in particular, can max-decisions-per-day be replaced by a measured MB-engine absorption capacity, and can flat-share=0.60 either be justified against the ~90% flow-trader rationale or moved?
findings.why_it_matters: These are HARD gates that permanently remove candidates (REJECT, not deepen). Thresholds tuned to admit one specific wallet are the definition of in-sample gate-fitting; a rebuild should either derive them from engine measurements or demote borderline bands to INSUFFICIENT.
findings.verify_note: Verified: the rework comments (:495-501, :1650-1653) justify the parameter set solely by 0xf705fa (461 fills/day, 7.6 decisions/day, 16% net-flat); no derivation is stated for 1000 (:1654-1657); the 25/day help text asserts engine absorption (:1658-1661) with no measured capacity anywhere in the file; flow_shape's own docstring says 'a true flow trader is ~90%+ flat' (:334) vs the 0.60 gate (:1662-1666) with no explanation of the gap. All secondary constants confirmed at the cited lines (100-fill floor :399-404, 20-position floor :414-418 with the test-documented no-ts_ok asymmetry at test :434-440, fabrication 0.50 :1644-1646, 10/0.80 :1641-1643, wash 0.50 :1648, tolerances :1636-1637). One word is arguably strong: 0.60 vs '~90%+' is an unexplained conservative margin rather than a strict logical contradiction, but the substantive point (unexplained gap, single-anecdote calibration) is accurate.

findings.title: decisions_per_day is a lifetime AVERAGE, not a peak-load measure — the copyability gate mis-measures what the engine must actually absorb
findings.detail: decisions_per_day = len(chain_first_buys) / max(span_days_frac, 1.0) over the trader's entire active span (chain_deep_dive.py:1117). A trader who enters 500 markets in a 10-day burst and is then dormant for a year averages ~1.4/day and passes the 25/day cap, though the copy engine would face ~50/day during bursts; conversely, a long-dormant trader recently accelerating is diluted the same way. The gate's stated purpose is engine absorption (:544-546), which is a peak/短-window constraint, not a lifetime-mean constraint. Same shape applies to the receipt-free rate (:1008).
findings.review_question: Should the rebuild measure decision rate on rolling windows (e.g. p95 of 7-day decision rate) instead of the lifetime mean, and has anyone measured how burst-shaped the admitted cohorts' entry streams actually are?
findings.why_it_matters: A copyability gate that can pass bursty traders and fail steady ones on the same true load answers the wrong question for a one-bet-per-market engine; the readout would then blame 'trader quality' for what is actually unabsorbed burst flow.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed: :1117 divides total chain first-buys by the full active span (span_days_frac from min..max fill blocks, 1-day floor); :544-546 states the gate's purpose as engine absorption; :1008 gives true_rate the same lifetime-mean shape. The burst arithmetic in the finding is correct (500 markets / ~370d span ≈ 1.35/day passes the 25/day cap despite ~50/day during the burst). No windowed/peak measure exists anywhere in the file.

findings.title: Sweep 'completeness' is proven only by absence of RPC errors plus a head-only canary — no positive control at historical depth; a served fill-cache additionally asserts rpc_err_frac=0.0
findings.detail: sweep_complete = rpc_err_frac <= 0.05 AND canary_ok AND n_chain_fills > 0 (chain_deep_dive.py:486-487, :1009-1010). The canary only checks that a ~20-block window near HEAD returns V2 fills (:821-834); an archive RPC that silently returns empty results for deep historical ranges (without erroring) would pass every leaf (leaf_ok counts successes regardless of emptiness, :684-686), leaving V1-era fills missing while the sweep reads complete — and Direction-A would then count old API BUYs as not_found, feeding the FABRICATION REJECT (:531-534) from an infrastructure artifact. When --fill-cache-dir serves a cached range it hard-codes leaf_fail=0 / rpc_err_frac=0.0 on the strength of a past run's cleanliness (chain_fill_cache.py:117-120), so current-run completeness partially rests on persist-time claims.
findings.review_question: Should the rebuild add a depth positive control — e.g. re-detect one known historical fill (from a prior verified verdict) at sweep start on the same RPC — before any FABRICATION verdict is allowed to stand?
findings.why_it_matters: FABRICATION is the screen's gravest accusation and it is structurally reachable from a silently-lossy archive endpoint. Whether tenderly's archive actually behaves this way is unmeasured — hence hypothesis — but the cost of the control is one getLogs call and it converts the screen's worst false-accusation mode into a detected infra failure.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed: sweep_complete = rpc_err_frac <= cap AND canary_ok AND fills>0 (:486-487, :1009-1010); canary checks only a ~20-block window ~60 blocks behind HEAD (:821-834); a successful-but-empty getLogs counts as leaf_ok (the increment is actually at :682-683 — the cited :684-686 is the adjacent except branch, a 1-2 line drift that doesn't change the mechanism); FABRICATION REJECT at :531-534; serve() hard-codes leaf_fail=0/rpc_err_frac=0.0 (chain_fill_cache.py:117-120), resting on the persist-time rule that only leaf_fail==0 sweeps are cached (module docstring :26-28). The silent-empty-archive failure mode is a fair inference: nothing distinguishes 'no fills existed' from 'RPC silently served nothing' at historical depth.

findings.title: ADMIT's 'no forensic flag' clause is weaker than it reads: copier probe off by default, hidden-activity report-only (and null on incomplete caches), wash detection blind to V1 and all taker fills
findings.detail: The ADMIT reason string says 'no forensic flag' (chain_deep_dive.py:586-590), but: (1) the copier/double-lag probe defaults to copier_sample=0 = skipped entirely (:1670-1671; :1122-1124), and MB_STATE records an ADMIT where 'the copier-forensic leg never ran' (docs/MB_STATE.md:373); (2) Direction-B hidden activity is deliberately report-only, and on an incomplete cache it is not computed at all (hidden=null, :1108-1112; docs/MB_STATE.md:374 'hidden=null != zero hidden'); (3) wash concentration only sees V2 maker-side fills because V1 counterparty is deliberately None (operator-matched, :159-163) and V2 taker fills carry no counterparty (:208-210) — a washer operating as taker or in the V1 era is invisible to it.
findings.review_question: Should ADMIT output enumerate which forensic legs actually RAN (copier: skipped / hidden: null / wash: V2-maker-only) instead of the blanket 'no forensic flag', and should the rebuild make the copier probe mandatory for admission given double-lag directly attacks copy profitability?
findings.why_it_matters: The operator reads the verdict string as the evidence summary. A rebuild decision about which forensics to keep needs to start from what the current ADMIT actually checked — which for the copier leg (the one forensic aimed squarely at copy-ability rather than trader integrity) has typically been nothing.
findings.verify_note: All three legs confirmed: ADMIT reason string 'no forensic flag' at :586-590; copier_sample default 0 = skipped (:1670-1671, gated at :1122-1124) with MB_STATE :373 recording an ADMIT where the copier leg never ran; Direction-B is comment-documented REPORT-ONLY (:1091-1098) and hidden=null on non-'ok' caches (:1099-1112) with MB_STATE :374's 'hidden=null ≠ zero hidden'; V1 counterparty deliberately None (:158-163) and V2 taker fills carry counterparty=None (:208-214), so counterparty_concentration (:359-372) cannot see a washer operating as taker or in the V1 era.

findings.title: Gate-version skew across cohorts: cohort-2's live ADMITs never faced the 2026-07-16 decision/flow gates, and the legacy 200/day gate survives only as a reporting flag
findings.detail: The copyability rules were reworked on 2026-07-16 (fix-not-bend: old hft_max_rate=200/day REJECT retired to 'reporting threshold only', chain_deep_dive.py:1667-1669; new receipt-free/decision/flow gates :495-501, :539-552). MB_STATE explicitly logs the open item: 'cohort-2's 8 live ADMITs never faced the new decision/flow gates — shadow measures copyability empirically (chosen for now); uniform re-dive = backlog' (docs/MB_STATE.md:936-938). Later cohorts (run-4 onward, cohort-5 eligibility) were screened under the new rules, so traders admitted under materially different admission semantics coexist in the lane's forward comparisons.
findings.review_question: Does the overhaul require a screen-version stamp on every verdict/cohort (and per-cohort readout separation by screen version), or a one-time uniform re-screen of all live roster members under the current gate set before any cross-cohort conclusion is drawn?
findings.why_it_matters: Forward readouts comparing cohorts admitted under different gate sets confound trader quality with admission-rule vintage. Since verdict locks are immutable, the rebuild has to decide how versioned admission rules and locked verdicts coexist — this is a governance question only the review can settle.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed: --hft-max-rate help text says 'LEGACY (2026-07-16): reporting threshold only — no longer rejects' (:1667-1669); the new receipt-free band (:495-506) and decision/flow hard gates (:539-552) verified; MB_STATE :936-938 carries the open item verbatim ('cohort-2's 8 live ADMITs never faced the new decision/flow gates — shadow measures copyability empirically (chosen for now); uniform re-dive = backlog'). Run-4 ran post-rework code (run-3 was killed partly BECAUSE it ran pre-rework code, MB_STATE :902-904) and cohort-5 eligibility draws on the ADMIT/re-review dirs, so mixed-semantics coexistence in forward comparisons is accurate.

findings.title: Cohort5's admission bar is structurally near-unclearable by the lane's own 08-19 power analysis, yet it is unchanged and was extended to new groups on 08-24
findings.detail: Cohort5 criteria (registered 07-30): forward edge >= +0.02 on >= 30 resolved AND per-trader P(>0) >= 0.95, single pre-registered look consumed at first crossing of 30. The 08-19 sequential-design analysis established: P>=0.95 at n=30 requires edge >= +0.127 (6.4x the floor); one-shot power at realistic edges is 7-8%; the full bar (edge>=+0.02 AND P>=0.95) can NEVER pass for true edge <= ~+0.022 (joint power caps ~0.49 at any n). The band test got the anytime-valid redesign; the cohort5 per-trader bar did not. Since then 5 of 20 single-look tests have been consumed as DOES-NOT-QUALIFY, and on 08-24 the 9 untested cohort1 traders were added under 'same bars' (fresh epoch 2026-08-24T17:00:00Z), with a 12-probe plan proposing the same bar again.
findings.review_question: Should the remaining 15 cohort5 looks and the 9 fresh cohort1-untested looks be paused and re-registered under an anytime-valid design (as the band was) before more one-shot tests are irreversibly consumed at 7-8% power? Was the 08-19 'the bar itself needs an operator redesign decision' question ever explicitly ruled for cohorts (only the band redesign is recorded as executed)?
findings.why_it_matters: The qualification funnel is the rebuild's roster-selection mechanism, and funding is gated on 'a test passes.' Burning each trader's single immutable test against a bar the lane itself proved near-impossible converts real edge (if any) into permanent DOES-NOT-QUALIFY locks — an irreversible cost accruing daily.

findings.title: Possible fee-equation drift between cohort5's registered charter (flat 2%) and the venue fee formula that went live in the readout stack on 08-19
