findings.title: Dual bot identity: MirrorBot vs MirrorBotV3 rows accrete concurrently in the same DB tables
findings.detail: mirror_v3 uses BOT_NAME='MirrorBotV3' precisely so 'old rows stay queryable but never mix in' (mirror_v3/__init__.py:12-13, :19), and run.py's restore SQL filters by that name (run.py:62-65, :71-75). Meanwhile legacy keeps writing trade_events/positions rows under 'MirrorBot' for its paper trades (finding 1). Both write into the same Postgres. Every canonical P&L read (scripts/bot_pnl.py <BotName>) and every guard-restore query is identity-scoped, so numbers labeled 'MB' are ambiguous until the identity is named. The shadow lane itself writes NO DB rows at all (copy_watcher.py docstring 'NO orders, no DB writes' :48-50) — its record is the JSONL sinks (shadow_path/rtds_sink/bidsim_path, WatcherConfig :335-351).
findings.review_question: At overhaul time, which identity inherits the future live track record — and does the review agenda need a standing rule that every reported MB number names its identity (MirrorBot legacy-paper vs MirrorBotV3 vs shadow-JSONL) plus the sink it came from?
findings.why_it_matters: The funding decision chain (band test, bidsim, cohort qualification) reads from JSONL sinks; legacy P&L reads from trade_events. Conflating the three sources is the exact denominator-mixing failure the operator's verification rules exist to prevent.
findings.verify_note: Citations are accurate (mirror_v3/__init__.py:12-13/:19; run.py:62-75 identity-scoped restore SQL; copy_watcher.py:48-50 'No orders (paper or live), no DB writes' and sink paths at :335-351; legacy place_order at :4396-4404). But the headline claim is wrong on the V3 half: nothing in the repo writes MirrorBotV3 rows — run.py:65/:75/:88 are SELECT-only, the strategy slot is empty, and the shadow/RTDS/bidsim lanes write JSONL only (as the finding's own detail concedes). Only legacy 'MirrorBot' rows can accrete; 'both accrete concurrently' is unsupported. The identity-ambiguity point for P&L reads is valid.

findings.title: The dormant order_gateway neg-risk landmine is a legacy-path-only hazard; mirror3's detection covers NegRiskExchange V2 natively and order-free
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md (worktree copy, 'DORMANT LANDMINE' section :21-25) codifies that order_gateway._can_exit's neg-risk BUY block silently no-ops for MirrorBot only because of a market-index key mismatch, and that 'repairing' the lookup would re-create Bug 14 (all elections/tournaments cut). This hazard exists solely on the legacy execution path (order_gateway is consulted on legacy's order flow). mirror3's shadow lane never routes orders at all, and its detection explicitly watches BOTH V2 exchanges including NegRiskExchange V2 (copy_watcher.py:98-99, address list at :516-517, single eth_getLogs over both at :540-548), so neg-risk roster fills are first-class signals with no gateway in the path.
findings.review_question: Should the overhaul schedule CLAUDE.md's option (a) — remove the dead gateway block entirely with operator signoff — as part of legacy retirement, so the landmine cannot outlive the only bot it endangers? And does the future v3 live execution path route through order_gateway at all (re-importing the hazard) or through a new executor?
findings.why_it_matters: The landmine is a standing tax: every future session must be warned not to fix an obvious-looking bug. Retirement is the one moment it can be removed safely; if v3's live executor reuses order_gateway, the neg-risk block must be neutralized first or Bug 14 ships again.
findings.verify_note: Worktree CLAUDE.md 'DORMANT LANDMINE' section sits at lines 21-25 with exactly the claimed content (market-index key mismatch makes the neg-risk BUY block no-op; repairing it re-creates Bug 14). copy_watcher.py:98-99 defines EXCHANGE_V2 + NEGRISK_EXCHANGE_V2, :516-517 builds the two-address list, :540-548 issues ONE eth_getLogs over both. The shadow lane places no orders (docstring :48-50), so no gateway is in its path. Claim matches the evidence.

findings.detail: deploy/polymarket-mirror3-shadow.service documents the split: code runs from /opt/mirror3, 'a persistent clone of the investigation branch carrying mirror_v3/copy_watcher.py', because 'the deployed v2 tree ... does not have the watcher'; the venv is shared packages-only, and the unit is to be 'replace[d] with the canonical unit when the branch merges to master'. findings.title: Both network runners — the chain poll loop and the RTDS websocket loop — have zero test coverage, and they are where every major live defect has occurred
findings.detail: The test suite's own docstring codifies the boundary: 'pure core only (the network runner is exercised on the VPS)'. watch() (copy_watcher.py:502-691) contains untested decision logic that is NOT network I/O: the cursor state machine (retry-don't-skip, fail_streak reset, cursor=lo vs hi+1, loud-skip after MAX_WINDOW_RETRIES at :586-611), canary scheduling wiring (:566-583), receipt-failure side=None skip (:627-642), and the JSONL sink append (:684-685). rtds_watch() (:790-958) contains the reconnect/backoff schedule, the 15s silent alarm, the PONG-vs-data-liveness split (:850-862), and the app-ping task lifecycle — all inline at ~7 nesting levels. The comments themselves document that this exact region shipped multiple live defects (:712-728: 83 silent alarms/13.9h, ~9.2% downtime, a refuted PING root-cause theory; :832-835: a silent app-ping death that hid whether PINGs were sent). A regression in any of this passes the suite silently because none of it is reachable from a test.
findings.review_question: Should the rebuild extract the cursor/retry state machine and the RTDS liveness/reconnect state machine into pure, offline-testable cores (the way evaluate_gates/canary_state/BidRegistry already are), so that the 'network runner tested on VPS' convention shrinks to genuinely untestable I/O edges?
findings.why_it_matters: Dropped windows and silently-dead subscriptions are lost forward samples — under FORWARD DATA ONLY those samples are the only decision evidence the lane produces, and the historical record shows this is precisely where the lane has bled before.
findings.verify_note: All cites verified: test docstring :1-2 'pure core only (the network runner is exercised on the VPS)'; watch() spans 502-691 with cursor machine/loud-skip at 586-611 (cursor=lo :609, hi+1 :607/:612), canary wiring 566-583, side=None skip 627-642, sink append 684-685; rtds_watch 790-958 with 15s alarm (RTDS_SILENT_ALARM_S=15 :718), backoff :719/:955-958, PONG-vs-data split 850-862, app-ping 823-837/949; defect history at 712-728 (83 alarms/13.9h, ~9.2% downtime, PING theory REFUTED) and 832-835. Greps confirm no test calls watch()/rtds_watch(). Sole caveat: 'every major live defect' is slightly broad — the $1.00-fill (PRICE_NO_UPSIDE) defect was a pure-core gate omission (copy_watcher.py:36-38, :252-256), though every documented outage/blindness defect did land in the runners.

findings.title: The entire readout/verdict pipeline (shadow_readout.py, analyze_shadow.py, band_tracker.py, cohort5_qualification.py) is invisible to pytest — its self-tests exist but are not wired into the suite
findings.detail: No file in tests/ imports shadow_readout, analyze_shadow, band_tracker, or cohort5_qualification (grep across tests/ returns nothing). Each script carries a rich --self-test (shadow_readout._self_test at scripts/shadow_readout.py:672 covers cohort split, ledger-drift refusal, concentration disclosure, post-hoc verdict-vocabulary refusal, label-supplement precedence, and locks), but it only runs when someone remembers to run it manually on the VPS. The repo already has the wiring pattern — tests/unit/test_readjudicate_discrepant.py:97-98 runs rd._self_test() under pytest — it just was never applied to the readout scripts. Consequence: a regression in the cohort-pooling guards, the DB-vs-supplement precedence, or the alert logic passes `pytest` completely green.
findings.review_question: Should the rebuild make wiring every script self-test into pytest a hard acceptance criterion (one-line wrappers per the readjudicate precedent), and should CI-green be redefined to include the readout layer before any verdict from it is trusted?
findings.why_it_matters: The readout IS the product of the shadow lane — it computes the pre-registered verdicts the money decision hangs on. A verdict machine whose regressions cannot fail the suite is a single manual step away from silently emitting a wrong SURVIVES/REJECT.
findings.verify_note: Grep across tests/ for the four module names returns zero matches (other scripts ARE imported: audit_roster_chain, readjudicate_discrepant). _self_test at shadow_readout.py:672 covers all six claimed areas (split ok1, ledger-drift refusal ok6 loop :818-874, concentration ok7-9/ok21, post-hoc vocabulary refusal ok16-18, label precedence ok22-25, locks ok26-29). Wiring pattern exists at test_readjudicate_discrepant.py:97-98 (assert rd._self_test() == 0). band_tracker.py:129 is its _self_test.

findings.title: Verdict-lock immutability — the stopping-rule enforcement — is tested only inside the un-wired self-test
findings.detail: LockError/load_locks/write_lock/locked_diag_reason (scripts/shadow_readout.py:406-448) implement the operator's stopping rule: one pre-registered test per cohort, consumed at first crossing, re-lock refused, corrupt lock file fatal (never silently {}). The only tests of this behavior are self-test checks ok26-ok29 (scripts/shadow_readout.py:1028-1060), which pytest never executes. band_tracker.py reuses these same lock helpers for the live band-forward test (scripts/band_tracker.py:27 imports shadow_readout), so a regression in write_lock's re-lock refusal would let a later run silently re-adjudicate a locked verdict — the optional-stopping hole the lock exists to close — with no suite signal.
findings.review_question: Given that verdict locks are declared immutable in the operator contract, should lock semantics get first-class pytest coverage (including the atomic os.replace write path and the corrupt-file raise) before the rebuild adds any new lock consumers?
findings.why_it_matters: Lock immutability is the mechanism that makes pre-registered epochs binding. If it can regress silently, every locked verdict in the durable log becomes revisable in practice, which invalidates the lane's entire anti-peeking guarantee.
findings.verify_note: LockError/load_locks/write_lock/locked_diag_reason at shadow_readout.py:406-448 exactly as described (re-lock refused :430-432, corrupt file raises never {} :417-424). Lock self-tests ok26-ok29 at :1028-1061 (cited 1028-1060, off by one line at most). band_tracker.py:27 imports shadow_readout and calls sr.load_locks(:93)/sr.write_lock(:121) for the live band test. Minor context: band_tracker also early-returns on an existing 'band_0.65_0.85' lock (:95-99), so the write_lock refusal is the backstop rather than the only defense — doesn't invalidate the claim.

findings.title: FirstBuyDedup is in-memory only — a watcher restart re-flags first buys, and the readout trusts the flag; no test covers restart semantics
findings.detail: The graded estimand is FIRST BUY per (trader, token). FirstBuyDedup (mirror_v3/copy_watcher.py:444-457) is a bare in-process set, instantiated fresh at :551 (chain) and :803 (RTDS); nothing rehydrates it from the sink. Contrast: the bidsim registry DOES rehydrate its _done set from its sink exactly to prevent double-registration across restarts (copy_watcher.py:1057-1098, tested at test_mirror3_copy_watcher.py:654-673). After any restart, a trader's later add-on buy on an already-recorded token is written with first_buy=true, and analyze_shadow trusts the flag as-is (scripts/analyze_shadow.py:188 'firsts = [r for r in records if r.get("first_buy")]'). The lane has restarted multiple times (TRUST2 at scripts/shadow_readout.py:54 is itself 'watcher restart epoch'). Token-clustered bootstrap dampens but does not remove the effect: duplicate first-buys inflate first_buys/OK-rate/tax counts and add within-cluster weight to the pooled edge. Magnitude is unmeasured.
findings.review_question: Measure on the live sink: how many (trader, token) pairs carry more than one first_buy=true record across restart epochs, and does re-deriving first-buy globally at readout time move any cohort's edge/P? Should the rebuild persist dedup (bidsim-style rehydration) or move dedup into the readout entirely?
findings.why_it_matters: This is a quiet estimand-integrity leak in the lane's primary dataset: the numbers feeding pre-registered verdicts may count non-first buys as first buys, and the readout's repair machinery never checks for it. Related: the cursor also initializes forward-only at head+1 (copy_watcher.py:552), so restart downtime is a permanent detection gap in the same dataset.
findings.verify_note: FirstBuyDedup at copy_watcher.py:444-457 is a bare in-process set with no rehydration; fresh instances at :551 (chain) and :803 (RTDS). Contrast confirmed: bidsim_rehydrate :1057-1098 seeds _done from its sink ('a restart can never double-register'), tested at test_mirror3_copy_watcher.py:654-673. analyze_shadow.py:188 is verbatim as quoted and trusts the flag. TRUST2 at shadow_readout.py:54 = 'watcher restart epoch'. Cluster-dampening claim checks out: analyze_shadow pools per-record within token clusters (:214-238, cluster_bootstrap_p :148), so duplicates inflate first_buys/vals and add within-cluster weight.

findings.title: run.py's state-restore SQL is never executed by any test — the silo tests inject fake loaders around it
findings.detail: TestRestoreOrdering (tests/unit/test_mirror_v3_silo.py:132-191) rigorously proves the fail-closed ordering contract, but only with injected async lambdas. The real loaders — fetch_entered (mirror_v3/run.py:57), fetch_open (run.py:68), fetch_daily_exposure (run.py:78) — carry inline SQL against trade_events/markets/positions whose column contracts (source_bot OR bot_id, is_paper, execution_mode, m.resolved) are never exercised anywhere in the suite. A schema drift or a wrong column name would boot-loop on the VPS but pass pytest green. Also INFERRED from reading the SQL: fetch_entered filters execution_mode = :mode (run.py:64) but fetch_daily_exposure has no mode filter at all (run.py:87 — bot_name + event_time only), so the daily-exposure restore would pool paper and live history if the identity ever ran both modes.
findings.review_question: Should the rebuild give the three loader queries either an integration test against a real schema (even a migration-built sqlite/pg fixture) or at minimum a column-contract test, and should fetch_daily_exposure's missing execution_mode filter be reconciled with fetch_entered's before any live flip?
findings.why_it_matters: State restore is the guard spine — the one-bet-per-market guarantee opens only on its full success. The proven part is the orchestration; the unproven part is the actual data contract, which is exactly where past MB bugs (S244 same-mode-history fix, referenced in run.py's own comment) lived.
findings.verify_note: fetch_entered :57 (execution_mode filter :64, m.resolved :63), fetch_open :68 (source_bot OR bot_id :72, is_paper :73), fetch_daily_exposure :78-89 with WHERE bot_name + event_time only (:87) — no mode filter, exactly as the INFERRED note states. TestRestoreOrdering at test_mirror_v3_silo.py:132-191 uses injected async lambdas only. The suite's sole import of mirror_v3.run (:197) tests the env guard before any DB work, so the loaders' SQL is never executed under pytest. Boot-loop mechanism grounded: restore failure returns 1 for systemd restart (run.py:92-96).

findings.title: Several guards are 'tested' by grepping source text rather than executing behavior — the suite's own history shows why that is fragile
findings.detail: test_bidsim_call_sites_pass_tx_through (tests/unit/test_mirror3_copy_watcher.py:626-643) asserts exact spellings like 'trigger_tx=row.get("tx")' appear in copy_watcher's source via inspect.getsource — its own comment admits an earlier spelling-based assert 'let a live 75%-inert guard through'. test_bug12_mode_flip_guard.py (tests/unit/test_bug12_mode_flip_guard.py:62-96) similarly asserts substrings exist in mirror_bot.py source. These tests pass if the code is dead/unreachable and fail on harmless renames; they verify text, not the runtime path. The pattern exists because the production call sites live inside the untestable network loops (finding 1) — the text-grep is a workaround for an architecture that cannot be invoked in a test.
findings.review_question: Should the rebuild treat every source-grep assertion as a marker of an architecture defect to close (make the call site injectable/testable, then replace the grep with a behavioral test), rather than carrying the pattern forward?
findings.why_it_matters: The lane's documented worst failure mode is 'a fix whose reporting path never adopts it' (inert guards). Text assertions detect only the spelling of adoption, not adoption itself — the exact class that already shipped a 75%-inert self-fill guard to live measurement.
findings.verify_note: test_bidsim_call_sites_pass_tx_through at test_mirror3_copy_watcher.py:626-643 asserts exact spellings via inspect.getsource; comment at :634-635 admits the earlier spelling assert 'let a live 75%-inert guard through'. test_bug12_mode_flip_guard.py:62-96 (and beyond) asserts substrings in mirror_bot source via inspect.getsource; its docstring (:46-50) concedes structural-presence testing because a full bootstrap is out of scope. Minor nuance: bug12's untestable call sites are MirrorBot's DB-bound scan paths rather than the copy_watcher network loops specifically, but the bidsim call sites do live in watch()/rtds_watch (:652-662, :899-918), so the architectural framing holds.

findings.title: The cron/deploy shell layer that actually runs the readouts daily is untested and carries a hard branch pin
findings.detail: deploy/shadow_readout_cron.sh pins BR=claude/repo-setup-docs-fq9bhn with a comment 'update when the MB lane moves branches'; on fetch failure it WARNs into the readout log and keeps running frozen code. deploy/label_and_fee_refresh_cron.sh chains four scripts (label supplement, fee map, cohort5 qualification, band tracker) with `set -uo pipefail` but per-block `tail -6`/`grep -E` output filters that can swallow mid-pipeline errors from the operator's view. No test of any kind touches these scripts, and their failure modes (branch moved, DATABASE_URL grep miss, venv path change) surface only as missing or stale readout lines. The alert-file lifecycle (existence = trigger, removed when no trigger, shadow_readout.py:660-668) is likewise only covered by the un-wired self-test path.
findings.review_question: Should the rebuild replace the branch-pin-in-cron pattern with a deploy-owned mechanism (e.g., the cron reading a pointer file the deploy script writes), and add a smoke check that the daily chain actually appended a readout line within N hours (a dead-man switch for the readout itself)?
findings.why_it_matters: The daily cron IS the lane's measurement heartbeat. A silently-frozen clone or a silently-failed chain step means verdict-relevant days pass with no data or stale code, and nothing in the test suite or the alert design would say so — the failure is only visible to a human reading the log.
findings.verify_note: shadow_readout_cron.sh:10 pins BR=claude/repo-setup-docs-fq9bhn with the exact 'update when the MB lane moves branches' comment; fetch failure WARNs into the readout log and keeps running frozen code (:17-21). label_and_fee_refresh_cron.sh has set -uo pipefail (:8) and per-block tail -6/tail -4/grep filters (:17,:20,:25,:30). No test references either script. Two conservative imprecisions: the refresh cron actually chains FIVE scripts (mb_scoreboard.py :32-35 is unnamed in the finding), and the alert-FILE lifecycle at shadow_readout.py:660-668 is in main() and not exercised even by _self_test (which covers only the alerts_for trigger logic) — actual coverage is slightly worse than claimed.

findings.title: Venue-semantics regression tests pin the ASSUMED endpoint behavior into mocks — a real venue-side change stays suite-green by construction

findings.title: Coverage accounting is structurally blind to the MB lane: pytest.ini measures only base_engine and bots, and a similarly-named test file covers a different bot's shadow system

findings.title: Pattern worth preserving: the pre-registered verdict table, boundary-derivation tests, and installed-library binding tests are the suite's strongest assets
findings.detail: Three patterns in the existing suite directly encode operator policy as executable contract and should survive any rebuild: (1) the deep-dive admission verdict table with every REJECT/INSUFFICIENT boundary asserted, including 'a lie beats incompleteness' ordering and 'gaps are never accusations' (tests/unit/test_chain_deep_dive.py:226-360); (2) flag-derivation tests at the exact pre-registered numeric boundaries, added after a review found earlier tests fed pre-computed flags into the verdict (test_chain_deep_dive.py:363-441 — a documented instance of a mock-asserting test being upgraded to a logic test); (3) tests binding against the INSTALLED web3 signature rather than a mock, born from a failure where mocked tests could not catch 580/580 silent rpc_errors (tests/unit/test_audit_roster_chain.py:97-121). The stress suite's seeded end-to-end conservation invariant (test_mirror3_stress.py:279-346) is the closest thing the lane has to a pipeline test and is the template for testing an extracted runner core.
findings.review_question: Does the rebuild plan explicitly carry these three patterns forward as requirements (policy-as-test, boundary-exact derivation tests, real-library binding), and apply the stress suite's conservation-invariant style to the newly extracted network-loop cores from finding 1?
findings.why_it_matters: An overhaul that only closes gaps can also destroy what works. These tests are where the suite has already caught or codified real money-relevant failures; losing them in a rewrite would be a regression the new suite could not detect about itself.

findings.title: Entire forward-evidence base is single-copy on the VPS - the only backup job covers the Postgres DB, on the same box
findings.detail: The lane's decision-bearing artifacts are all flat files under /opt/pa2-shared: mirror3_shadow.jsonl (canonical shadow sink), mirror3_shadow_rtds.jsonl, mirror3_bidsim.jsonl (+ the two parked pre-amend epochs), mb_copyable_data/chain_audit.json (roster ledger), copyable_cache/* (per-trader histories, gamma_resolutions.json, fee_map.json, fee_rate_map.json, chain_fills/), deep_dive*/ (verdict JSONs, shadow_readout_log.txt durable log, verdict_locks.json, band_lock.json, cohort5_qual_locks.json), rtds_scout/scout_20260730.jsonl. The only scheduled backup is deploy/daily_backup.sh - a pg_dump of the polymarket DB into /opt/pa2-backups on the SAME machine, 7-day retention (crontabs/postgres.crontab:6). The .bak siblings sessions create (chain_audit.json.pre-cohort4-20260730, mirror3_bidsim.jsonl.pre-amend1-20260821, etc.) are same-disk copies. Under the FORWARD DATA ONLY rule, these files ARE the totality of admissible evidence (docs/MB_STATE.md explicitly rules 'where they differ the durable log is the record'); a disk loss erases every pre-registered epoch's accrual, every immutable lock, and the durable log that reproduces the locks.

Weeks of pre-registered accrual (band epoch, bidsim epoch 2, cohort5/cohort1-untested windows) and the immutable verdict locks vanish with one VPS failure. findings.title: The canonical loader silently drops ANY undecodable line, not just torn tails - mid-file corruption of the evidence base would be invisible
findings.detail: analyze_shadow.load_records catches json.JSONDecodeError and continues on every line, commented as 'torn tail line from a live writer is expected' (analyze_shadow.py:60-63) - but the tolerance applies to the whole file, and no skip-count is returned or printed by the consumers that matter (band_tracker, cohort5, shadow_readout all call it bare). A partially-corrupted sink (disk pressure, concurrent epoch mv, editor accident on the single copy) would shrink the forward sample silently, biasing e-values and qualification windows with no alarm. Contrast: mb_scoreboard's bidsim section does count parse_fail (mb_scoreboard.py:70-73, printed :126-128), and the lane's own doctrine ('empty-set false-pass class', fail-LOUD guards) is applied to empty inputs but not to partially-readable ones.
findings.review_question: Should the overhaul require every sink read to report (and alarm on) skipped-line counts and/or carry per-line integrity (sequence numbers or a daily line-count/checksum manifest), so a shrunken evidence base is detectable?
findings.why_it_matters: The lane's entire epistemic contract is 'the sink is the record'. A record that can lose lines without anyone noticing undermines every instrument reading it - and unlike the empty-set case, which the lane already guards loudly, the partial-loss case has no guard at all today.
findings.verify_note: analyze_shadow.py:60-63 catches json.JSONDecodeError with continue on every line ('torn tail line from a live writer is expected'), returns no skip count; band_tracker:82-83 and cohort5:112-113 guard only EMPTY input (assert recs), shadow_readout:478 calls it bare — exactly the empty-vs-partial asymmetry claimed. Contrast confirmed: mb_scoreboard's bidsim section counts parse_fail (:70-73) and prints it (:126-128).

findings.title: Verdict locks are fragmented across three plain-JSON files whose immutability is enforced only by the writing code path
findings.detail: Three lock stores exist under deep_dive/: verdict_locks.json (cohort stopping rule, shadow_readout.py:1093-1095), band_lock.json (band_tracker.py:176-178), cohort5_qual_locks.json (cohort5_qualification.py:234-236, also holding the cohort1-untested single-looks per MB_STATE 08-24). findings.title: copyable_cache per-trader histories carry a silent staleness trap: chain_deep_dive's cache-hit short-circuit will reuse stale/truncated caches, and a partial pull becomes a permanent 'complete' record
findings.detail: The per-address API history caches under copyable_cache (built by find_copyable_traders.py) are reused by walkforward_copy_traders, backtest_copyable_fills, audit_roster_chain, readjudicate_discrepant, probe_ob_coverage, the watcher's conviction-median seeding (copy_watcher.py:518-526), and chain_deep_dive - which short-circuits on cache hit (documented at MB_STATE: chain_deep_dive.py:1283-1291) so 2026-07-10-era caches truncated at 500 rows with status='hft' silently fed dives, producing verdicts with incomplete_cache_sweep=TRUE. The lane's own landmine list adds: 'Never cache a partial pull ... it silently becomes a complete record and corrupts every later run' (MB_COPYTRADER_CONTEXT.md section 5). The separate chain_fills/ sub-cache got this right - written only from sweeps with leaf_fail==0, served only when fully covering the requested range (chain_fill_cache.py:26-30). The API caches have no equivalent freshness/completeness contract.

findings.title: The +0.02 econ floor has no computation anywhere in the docs, mismatches the current fee model, and is proven never to bind
findings.detail: The floor appears as given in the walk-forward FAIL rule (MB_COPYTRADER_CONTEXT.md:88-90), the shadow readout criteria (MB_STATE.md:1376-1379), cohort bars, and the band economic gate (BAND_PREREGISTRATION.md:30-33). But the fee model has since moved to the venue formula rate*p*(1-p), validated against live charged fees (MB_STATE.md:555-560), under which cost mid-band is ~0.7-1.2c, not 2c - the floor was never re-derived. Separately, the 08-19 sequential analysis ESTABLISHED the floor is 'decorative - it never binds' (P>=0.95 at n=30 requires edge >= +0.127; P-only and full-bar FPRs identical at 5.40%; MB_STATE.md:419-427).

findings.why_it_matters: The floor is the single number that converts a statistical result into a money decision across every instrument (band gate, cohort bars, sizing tiers). If it is simultaneously unfounded, stale against the fee model, and non-binding, the lane's profitability criterion is effectively undefined.
findings.verify_note: Citations verified: floor in walk-forward FAIL rule (MB_COPYTRADER_CONTEXT.md:88-90), readout criteria (MB_STATE.md:1375-1378), band gate (BAND_PREREGISTRATION.md:31-33); '2% haircut roughly RIGHT' (:222-227); S244 ~0.02/$1 (MIRRORBOT_FILTER_AUDIT_S244.md:189); venue formula validated (:555-562); 'DECORATIVE — IT NEVER BINDS' with +0.127/5.40% (:419-426). findings.title: Cap 0.98 (PRICE_NO_UPSIDE max_fill) is a number derived from the superseded flat-2% fee model, kept by operator ruling after both rationales weakened
findings.detail: The cap was deployed 08-19 as 'the zero-upside bound at the flat 2% fee' (MB_STATE.md:485-490), responding to a real defect - 8.6% of OK first-buys filled >=0.999, and fills >=0.90 measured NET -0.0233 P=0.000 under flat fee (MB_STATE.md:402-411, :525-527). After the venue fee formula landed, both rationales were explicitly re-examined: fills at exactly 1.000 remain guaranteed-nonpositive, but 0.98-0.99 became 'merely terrible risk/reward, not deterministic loss', and the >=0.90 stratum re-priced to -0.0092 P=0.216 - 'NO LONGER proven-negative under true fees' (MB_STATE.md:569-575). Operator RULED 2026-08-19: KEEP AS IS (0.98) (MB_STATE.md:575). So the current cut point is an operator-fiat number whose derivation belongs to a dead fee model; under the venue formula the zero-upside bound at p=0.98 would compute differently (fee ~0.1c at 0.98, not 2c).
findings.review_question: At rebuild, should max_fill be re-derived as the price where venue-fee-adjusted expected upside crosses zero (price-dependent), and does the gate's block volume (92 blocks/~3h, MB_STATE.md:638-639, virtually all whale-0.999 fills) tell us those blocks cost nothing - or is the 0.98-0.99 stratum excluding measurable positive flow?
findings.why_it_matters: The cap defines the tradable price universe forward. A cut point inherited from a superseded cost model silently shapes every forward instrument's sample (band excluded anyway, but cohort edges and OK-rates include the 0.85-0.98 region).
findings.verify_note: All verified: deployed as 'the zero-upside bound at the flat 2% fee' (MB_STATE.md:486-489); defect 8.6% >=0.999 of 3,257 OK first-buys (:403-404); >=0.90 stratum -0.0233 P=0.000 flat-fee (:525-526); re-examination under venue formula with 'merely terrible risk/reward, not deterministic loss' and -0.0092 P=0.216 'NO LONGER proven-negative' (:569-575); 'RULED 2026-08-19: KEEP AS IS (0.98)' (:575). The venue-formula fee at p=0.98 is ~0.10-0.14c (rate 0.04-0.07 x 0.98 x 0.02), so 'would compute differently' is arithmetically sound. The finding fairly credits the underlying defect as real.

findings.title: The funding ruling ($500 pilot -> ~$5,000) has no EV computation attached, and no document computes the lane's revenue ceiling under ANY success scenario
findings.detail: The ruling: 'start ~$500 once a test passes; grow to ~$5,000 as it proves out live' (MB_STATE.md:52-54) closes the long-open 'conditional funding number' (MB_STATE.md:616-617) - but neither the ruling nor any doc states what the money is expected to earn. Sketch from the docs' own numbers (INFERRED arithmetic, in-sample flow inputs): if ONLY the band test passes at the +0.02 economic gate, band accrual ~4 resolved markets/day (BAND_PREREGISTRATION.md:47-48) x $300/bet cap (MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md:19) x 0.02 = ~$24/day gross ceiling at full deployment - and $5,000 bankroll cannot even fund 4x$300/day at multi-day resolution horizons without recycling capital. At the $500 pilot the same arithmetic scales to ~$2-3/day. The whole-roster alternative (71.6 mkts/day, MB_STATE.md:510-511) at the floor edge would be ~$430/day gross, but the best in-sample pooled net is +0.00645 (MB_STATE.md:509-510) and the bar analysis says >=+0.02 pooled cannot even be proven below true ~+0.022 (MB_STATE.md:513-518). Fee already consumes 59.8% of gross in the only decomposition made (MB_STATE.md:520-523). No doc reconciles the build effort against these ceilings.
findings.review_question: What is the pre-registered revenue model of the funded lane: expected $/day at $500 and at $5,000, per success scenario (band-only pass vs cohort5 qualifiers vs both), using forward flow and forward edge at decision time? Does ~$24/day gross at full scale justify the rebuild, or does the plan require roster/flow growth that should itself be a named experiment?
findings.why_it_matters: This is the money-making lens the task asks for: every current experiment succeeding still bounds the lane at tens of dollars a day under the documented flow and floor. If the overhaul's implicit thesis is 'scale flow later', that thesis is currently unmeasured and unregistered - the decision-relevant gap is the absence of any EV computation next to the funding commitment.
findings.verify_note: Ruling verified verbatim (MB_STATE.md:52-55) closing the open item at :616-617. Grep across docs/ confirms no EV or revenue-ceiling computation attached to funding anywhere. The sketch arithmetic is correct on the docs' own inputs (4/day x $300 x 0.02 = $24/day; 71.6 x $300 x 0.02 ≈ $430/day) and the finding labels it INFERRED with in-sample flow inputs; supporting cites (+0.00645 :509, ~+0.022 never-provable :513-516, fee 59.8% :520-523, $300 cap MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md:19, 4/day BAND_PREREGISTRATION.md:47-48) all check. Ceiling assumes cap-size bets per band market — presented as a ceiling, which is consistent.

findings.title: The chosen sizing rule (A+D hybrid) is conditioned on a now-voided in-sample PASS; its multiplier values are operator-fiat; the Option D test has never been reported
findings.detail: MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md's decision record fixes A+D: flat 1-unit base + conviction multiplier 1.0x/1.25x/1.5x at r=2/4 thresholds, 'operator-set 2026-07-11', locked blind to data (MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md:113-131). Three problems for a rebuild: (1) the document's context conditions everything on 'walk-forward PASS (+0.0237 pooled, pre-cost)' (MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md:10-11) - an in-sample number now carrying zero decision weight; the conditioning field 'Readout verdict it was conditioned on: ____' is still blank (MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md:132). (2) The 'unit' is defined as BotBankrollManager fractional Kelly at 'the roster's pooled post-cost edge' (MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md:33-34) - which forward is currently negative (band -0.0685, MB_STATE.md:105) or in-sample near-zero (+0.00645, MB_STATE.md:509), making the Kelly unit ~zero or undefined. (3) Option D's adoption test (pooled Spearman rho>0, P>=0.95, >=100 resolved fills; MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md:96-98,127-131) was pre-registered 2026-07-11 and shipped to the watcher (conviction_r recorded per record, :123-125), yet no evaluation of it appears anywhere in MB_STATE.md despite months of shadow data.
findings.review_question: Has the Option D Spearman test ever been run on the accumulated shadow data (it is evaluable today at $0)? Does the sizing decision record get re-registered against forward evidence, and what does 1 unit equal when the pooled forward edge is <=0 - is there a floor unit, or does sizing rationally output zero (i.e. do not fund)?
findings.why_it_matters: Sizing is where EV becomes dollars. A rebuild that inherits a sizing rule conditioned on voided evidence, with fiat multipliers and an unevaluated add-on test, will produce bet sizes no one can defend; and if honest Kelly at measured forward edge is ~zero, that IS the sizing model's funding verdict.
findings.verify_note: Decision record with 1.0/1.25/1.5 at r=2/4 'operator-set 2026-07-11', locked blind, shipped with conviction_r per record (MB_SIZING_OPTIONS.md:113-131); context line 'walk-forward PASS (+0.0237 pooled, pre-cost)' (:10); blank conditioning field (:132); unit = fractional Kelly at 'the roster's pooled post-cost edge' (:33-34); D's test spec (:96-98, :127-131). Do not act on this', :965-968), not the test. Minor context: the doc formally conditions implementation on a SURVIVES shadow readout (:7-8), consistent with the blank field the finding cites. Band -0.0685 (:105) and +0.00645 (:509) check; the Kelly-unit-~zero inference is fair.

findings.title: Roster economics: the expensive chain deep-dive screen selects on a quantity the lane itself measured to NOT predict copy edge
findings.detail: The lane's core structural finding, stated in its own pre-registration: 'whale chain edge does not predict our copy edge' - all 20 ADMITs survived complete labels at chain +0.0101->+0.0749, yet copies measured near zero, with per-trader spread from chain +0.0199/copy -0.0432 to copy +0.08 (COHORT5_PREREGISTRATION.md:15-25; diagnostics MB_STATE.md:229-235). The screen is retained as fraud/skill gate (COHORT5_PREREGISTRATION.md:24-25, 33-34) at ~2.2h/trader dive cost (MB_STATE.md:295) plus receipt budgets (30,000 receipts hit a wall on one scout, MB_STATE.md:121-123). Roster stands at 31 = 15+8+6+1+1probe (MB_STATE.md:207); the proposed 12-probe expansion (roster 31->43) awaits explicit operator confirm (MB_STATE.md:72-76). Meanwhile the winner's-curse analysis found no detectable per-trader signal at current n in the copy data either (MB_STATE.md:529-534) - so neither chain edge nor current shadow n can yet rank traders.
findings.review_question: In a rebuild, what is the deep-dive screen's job description and unit cost budget, given it screens fraud but not profitability? Should roster growth (the main flow/revenue lever) run on a cheaper fraud-only screen with copy-edge selection left entirely to forward qualification - and what roster SIZE does the revenue model actually require?
findings.why_it_matters: Roster size drives flow, flow drives every instrument's time-to-verdict and the lane's revenue ceiling. The current admission pipeline spends its budget measuring a non-predictive quantity while the binding constraint everywhere is forward sample accrual.
findings.verify_note: Core structural finding quoted accurately (COHORT5_PREREGISTRATION.md:15-25, incl. chain +0.0199/copy -0.0432 and copy +0.08; diagnostics MB_STATE.md:229-233); screen retained as fraud/skill gate (COHORT5:24-25, 33-34) — which the finding fairly discloses; ~2.2h/trader (:295); 30,000-receipt wall (actually at :119-120, cited :121-123 — trivial offset); roster 31=15+8+6+1+1probe (:206, cited :207); 12-probe expansion awaiting confirm (:72-76); winner's-curse 'no detectable per-trader signal at current n' (:528-534). All claims match the docs' own statements.

findings.title: Scout-filter and copyability-gate numbers are unmeasured choices; the first filter provably selected only machines
findings.detail: Filter history: sweep #1's selection (notional >=$250k + >=100 markets + >=500 trades/6h) returned 9/9 machines and 0 admits - the state doc itself calls this 'a finding about the FILTER' (MB_STATE.md:115-127); the fix discovered the old floor (>=500 trades/6h = 2,000/day) sat ABOVE the 1,000/day UNCOPYABLE ceiling, so it 'could only EVER select machines' (MB_STATE.md:56-60). The replacement band (notional>=$25k / markets>=5 / 10<=n<250 per 6h) dry-ran to 82 human-scale candidates (MB_STATE.md:59-61) but its specific numbers carry no stated measurement basis. Upstream, the copyability params themselves - receipt-free REJECT >1,000 fills/day, decisions/day <=25, flat-share <0.60 - were 'pre-registered BEFORE any re-run' (MB_STATE.md:1198-1204) but no doc derives 25 or 0.60 from a measurement. Scout cadence remains an open operator decision (MB_STATE.md:60-61, :123-125).
findings.review_question: Which candidate-funnel thresholds are load-bearing enough to deserve derivation from the 07-30 firehose capture's actual wallet distribution (26,123 wallets measured, MB_STATE.md:59) rather than round numbers - and what does the funnel's yield curve (candidates surviving per threshold setting) look like before committing a sweep cadence?
findings.why_it_matters: The candidate funnel is the lane's growth engine, and it has already demonstrated a mode where a threshold choice made the desired outcome structurally impossible (9/9 machines). A rebuild should not re-inherit unexamined round numbers at the top of the funnel.
findings.verify_note: Verified: sweep #1 9 machines / 0 admits, 'a finding about the FILTER' (MB_STATE.md:115-124); old floor 2,000/day above the 1,000/day UNCOPYABLE ceiling, 'could only EVER select machines' (:56-59); new band dry-run 82 candidates (:59-61); copyability params 25/0.60 'pre-registered BEFORE any re-run' with no stated derivation (:1198-1204); cadence open (:61, :124). findings.title: EV language appears in rulings without any computation behind it - exemplar: the 'positive EV -> add' ruling on 13 INSUFFICIENTs that contain zero edge measurements
findings.detail: The operator ruled the 13 INSUFFICIENTs 'positive EV -> add, negative -> remove'; the session's finding: 'their dive verdicts contain NO edge measurement at all... verified across all 13 JSONs - no edge_mean/n_labeled fields', one is a duplicate already on the roster, and forward EV requires WATCHING them - hence the proposed 12 observation-only probes, still awaiting explicit confirm (MB_STATE.md:68-76). This is the clean instance of a broader pattern the review should inventory: decisions phrased in EV terms (funding trigger 'once a test passes' MB_STATE.md:52-54; scaling 'as it proves out live') where the EV quantity is unmeasured or the passing test's economic content is the non-binding +0.02 gate. The lane's process correctly caught this instance; the review question is whether the decision protocol should REQUIRE a computed EV line (forward edge x flow x size, or 'UNAVAILABLE') attached to every add/remove/fund proposal.
findings.review_question: Should the overhaul codify an 'EV line or UNAVAILABLE' requirement on every roster and funding proposal (mirroring the CLASS-NOT-INSTANCE discipline), so that 'positive EV' can never again be asked of an artifact that measures no EV?
findings.why_it_matters: The lane's verdict discipline is strong on statistics but the money layer (what a decision is expected to EARN) has no equivalent standing artifact; this ruling shows operator decisions are being requested and made in EV vocabulary the underlying data cannot support.
findings.verify_note: The exemplar is verified nearly verbatim at MB_STATE.md:68-76: ruling quoted, 'NO edge measurement at all... verified across all 13 JSONs — no edge_mean/n_labeled fields', duplicate 0x44886115 already rostered (real set 12), 12 observation-only probes proposed, awaiting explicit confirm. Funding-trigger cite (:52-54) checks. One caution: calling the +0.02 gate 'non-binding' extends the n=30-bar 'never binds' result to the band's post-rejection economic gate, where bindingness was not established — minor overreach in the generalization, not in the exemplar.

findings.title: List (b) synthesis: complete inventory of commitments lacking a supporting measurement

findings.why_it_matters: This is the requested list (b) in one place. The overhaul's cheapest wins are the fiat numbers already answerable from collected shadow/bidsim/fee data without any new instrument or spend.
